5.90.s:
.. ṛṣaya ūcuḥ .. ..
agnitīrthaṃ tvayā proktaṃ brahmatīrthaṃ ca yatpurā ..
na tayoḥ kathitotpattirmāhātmyaṃ ca mahāmate .. 1 ..
5.90.d:
.. ऋषय ऊचुः .. ..
अग्नितीर्थं त्वया प्रोक्तं ब्रह्मतीर्थं च यत्पुरा ..
न तयोः कथितोत्पत्तिर्माहात्म्यं च महामते .. 1 ..
5.90.m: The seers said: / As Agnitīrtha and Brahmatīrtha were mentioned by you previously, / yet their origin and māhātmya have not been told, O wise one;

5.90.s:
tasmādvistarato brūhi ekaikasya pṛthakpṛthak ..
na vayaṃ tṛptimāpannāḥ śṛṇvataste vaco'mṛtam .. 2 ..
5.90.d:
तस्माद्विस्तरतो ब्रूहि एकैकस्य पृथक्पृथक् ..
न वयं तृप्तिमापन्नाः शृण्वतस्ते वचोऽमृतम् .. 2 ..
5.90.m: therefore, speak of each one separately in detail; / we have not attained satiety hearing your nectar-like speech.

5.90.s:
.. sūta uvāca .. ..
atra vaḥ kīrtayiṣyāmi kathāṃ pātakanāśinīm ..
agnitīrthasamudbhūtāṃ sarvasaukhyāvahāṃ śubhām.. 3 ..
5.90.d:
.. सूत उवाच .. ..
अत्र वः कीर्तयिष्यामि कथां पातकनाशिनीम् ..
अग्नितीर्थसमुद्भूतां सर्वसौख्यावहां शुभाम्.. 3 ..
5.90.m: Sūta said: / Here I shall proclaim to you the story that destroys sins, / arising from Agnitīrtha, auspicious, bringing all happiness.

5.90.s:
somavaṃśasamudbhūtaḥ pratīpo nāma bhūpatiḥ ..
purāsīcchauryasaṃpanno brahmajñānavicakṣaṇaḥ.. 4 ..
5.90.d:
सोमवंशसमुद्भूतः प्रतीपो नाम भूपतिः ..
पुरासीच्छौर्यसंपन्नो ब्रह्मज्ञानविचक्षणः.. 4 ..
5.90.m: Formerly there was a king named Pratīpa, born in the lunar dynasty, / endowed with valour and skilled in the knowledge of Brahman.

5.90.s:
tasya putradvayaṃ jajñe sarvalakṣaṇalakṣitam ..
devāpiḥ prathamastatra dvitīyaḥ śaṃtanurdvijāḥ .. 5 ..
5.90.d:
तस्य पुत्रद्वयं जज्ञे सर्वलक्षणलक्षितम् ..
देवापिः प्रथमस्तत्र द्वितीयः शंतनुर्द्विजाः .. 5 ..
5.90.m: Two sons, endowed with all auspicious marks, were born to him: / Devāpi was the first among them, and the second was Śaṃtanu, O twice-born.

5.90.s:
atho śivapadaṃ prāpte pratīpe nṛpasattame ..
tapo'rthaṃ rājyamutsṛjya devāpirniyaryau vanam .. 6 ..
5.90.d:
अथो शिवपदं प्राप्ते प्रतीपे नृपसत्तमे ..
तपोऽर्थं राज्यमुत्सृज्य देवापिर्नियर्यौ वनम् .. 6 ..
5.90.m: Then, when that best of kings, Pratīpa, attained the state of Śiva, / Devāpi, having renounced the kingdom, departed to the forest for the sake of austerity.

5.90.s:
tataśca maṃtribhiḥ sarvaiḥ śaṃtanustasya cānujaḥ ..
pitṛpaitāmahe rājye satvaraṃ sanniyojitaḥ .. 7 ..
5.90.d:
ततश्च मंत्रिभिः सर्वैः शंतनुस्तस्य चानुजः ..
पितृपैतामहे राज्ये सत्वरं सन्नियोजितः .. 7 ..
5.90.m: And then Śaṃtanu, his younger brother, was quickly established / by all the ministers in the ancestral kingdom.

5.90.s:
etasminnaṃtare śakro na vavarṣa kruddhā'nvitaḥ ..
yāvaddvādaśavarṣāṇi tasmi nrājyaṃ praśāsati .. 8 ..
5.90.d:
एतस्मिन्नंतरे शक्रो न ववर्ष क्रुद्धाऽन्वितः ..
यावद्द्वादशवर्षाणि तस्मि न्राज्यं प्रशासति .. 8 ..
5.90.m: In the meantime, Indra, filled with wrath, did not rain / for twelve years while he ruled the kingdom.

5.90.s:
ataḥ kṛcchraṃ gataḥ sarvo lokaḥ kṣutparipīḍitaḥ ..
cāmuṃḍāsadṛśo jāto yo na mṛtyuvaśaṃgataḥ .. 9 ..
5.90.d:
अतः कृच्छ्रं गतः सर्वो लोकः क्षुत्परिपीडितः ..
चामुंडासदृशो जातो यो न मृत्युवशंगतः .. 9 ..
5.90.m: Consequently, all the people fell into distress, afflicted by hunger; / whoever did not fall into the power of death became like Cāmuṇḍā.

5.90.s:
saṃtyaktāḥ patibhirnāryaḥ putrāśca pitṛbhirnijaiḥ ..
mātaraśca tathā putrairlokeṣvanyeṣu kā kathā .. 6.90.10 ..
5.90.d:
संत्यक्ताः पतिभिर्नार्यः पुत्राश्च पितृभिर्निजैः ..
मातरश्च तथा पुत्रैर्लोकेष्वन्येषु का कथा .. 6.90.10 ..
5.90.m: Wives were abandoned by husbands, and sons by their own fathers; / and so mothers by sons—what to say of other people?

5.90.s:
daivayogātkvacitkiṃcitkasyacidyadi dṛśyate ..
sasyaṃ siddhamasiddhaṃ vā hriyate vīryataḥ paraiḥ .. 11 ..
5.90.d:
दैवयोगात्क्वचित्किंचित्कस्यचिद्यदि दृश्यते ..
सस्यं सिद्धमसिद्धं वा ह्रियते वीर्यतः परैः .. 11 ..
5.90.m: If by chance anywhere anything was seen belonging to anyone, / grain, whether cooked or uncooked, it was seized by force by others.

5.90.s:
śuṣkā mahīruhāḥ sarve tathā ye ca jalāśayāḥ..
nadyaśca svalpatoyāśca gaṃgādyā api saṃsthitāḥ .. 12 ..
5.90.d:
शुष्का महीरुहाः सर्वे तथा ये च जलाशयाः..
नद्यश्च स्वल्पतोयाश्च गंगाद्या अपि संस्थिताः .. 12 ..
5.90.m: All the trees dried up, and likewise whatever reservoirs of water there were; / and rivers, even the Gaṅgā and others, were reduced to very little water.

5.90.s:
evaṃ vṛṣṭeḥ kṣaye jāte naṣṭe dharmapathe tathā ..
loke'sminnasthisaṃghātaiḥ pūrite bhasmanā vṛte .. 13 ..
5.90.d:
एवं वृष्टेः क्षये जाते नष्टे धर्मपथे तथा ..
लोकेऽस्मिन्नस्थिसंघातैः पूरिते भस्मना वृते .. 13 ..
5.90.m: When such failure of rain had occurred and the path of dharma was lost, / this world was filled with heaps of bones and covered with ash.

5.90.s:
na kaścidyajanaṃ cakre na svādhyāyaṃ na ca vratam ..
evamālokyate vyoma vṛṣṭyarthaṃ kṣutsamākulaiḥ .. 14 ..
5.90.d:
न कश्चिद्यजनं चक्रे न स्वाध्यायं न च व्रतम् ..
एवमालोक्यते व्योम वृष्ट्यर्थं क्षुत्समाकुलैः .. 14 ..
5.90.m: No one performed sacrifices, nor private Vedic study, nor vows; / thus the sky was looked upon for rain by those overwhelmed with hunger.

5.90.s:
etasminneva kāle tu viśvāmitro mahāmuniḥ ..
carmāsthiśeṣasarvāṃgo bubhukṣārta itastataḥ .. 15 ..
5.90.d:
एतस्मिन्नेव काले तु विश्वामित्रो महामुनिः ..
चर्मास्थिशेषसर्वांगो बुभुक्षार्त इतस्ततः .. 15 ..
5.90.m: At that very time, the great sage Viśvāmitra, / whose entire body was reduced to skin and bones, afflicted by hunger, [wandered] here and there.

5.90.s:
paribhramaṃstataḥ prāpya kaṃcidgrāmaṃ nirudvasam ..
mṛtamartyodbhavaivyāptamasthisaṃghaiḥ samaṃtataḥ .. 16 ..
5.90.d:
परिभ्रमंस्ततः प्राप्य कंचिद्ग्रामं निरुद्वसम् ..
मृतमर्त्योद्भवैव्याप्तमस्थिसंघैः समंततः .. 16 ..
5.90.m: Wandering about, he then reached a certain deserted village, / filled all around with heaps of bones originating from dead mortals.

5.90.s:
atha tatra bhramanprāptaścaṃḍālasya niveśanam..
śūnye go'sthisamākīrṇe durgaṃdhena samāvṛte .. 17 ..
5.90.d:
अथ तत्र भ्रमन्प्राप्तश्चंडालस्य निवेशनम्..
शून्ये गोऽस्थिसमाकीर्णे दुर्गंधेन समावृते .. 17 ..
5.90.m: Then, wandering there, he arrived at the dwelling of an outcaste, / empty, strewn with cattle bones, and enveloped in a foul stench.

5.90.s:
athāpaśyanmṛtaṃ tatra sārameyaṃ ciroṣitam ..
saṃśuṣkaṃ gandhanirmuktaṃ gṛhaprāṃte vyavasthitam .. 19 ..
samādāya tatastaṃ ca āpaddharmaparāyaṇaḥ ..
prakṣālya salile paścātpracakarta tadā muniḥ .. 19 ..
5.90.d:
अथापश्यन्मृतं तत्र सारमेयं चिरोषितम् ..
संशुष्कं गन्धनिर्मुक्तं गृहप्रांते व्यवस्थितम् .. 19 ..
समादाय ततस्तं च आपद्धर्मपरायणः ..
प्रक्षाल्य सलिले पश्चात्प्रचकर्त तदा मुनिः .. 19 ..
5.90.m:
Then he saw there a dead dog that had lain there for a long time, / thoroughly dried up, devoid of smell, lying at the edge of the house.
Then, having taken it up, intent on the conduct permissible in distress, / and having washed it afterwards in water, the sage cut it into pieces.

5.90.s:
tataśca śrapayāmāsa susamiddhe hutāśane ..
kṣutkṣāmo bhojanārthāya tataḥ pākāgrameva ca .. 6.90.20 ..
5.90.d:
ततश्च श्रपयामास सुसमिद्धे हुताशने ..
क्षुत्क्षामो भोजनार्थाय ततः पाकाग्रमेव च .. 6.90.20 ..
5.90.m: And then, emaciated by hunger, he cooked it on a well-kindled fire / for the sake of eating; then, having taken the first portion of the cooked food,

5.90.s:
samādāya pitṝṃstarpya yāvadagnau juhoti saḥ ..
tāvadvahniḥ parityajya samastamapi bhūtalam .. 21 ..
5.90.d:
समादाय पितॄंस्तर्प्य यावदग्नौ जुहोति सः ..
तावद्वह्निः परित्यज्य समस्तमपि भूतलम् .. 21 ..
5.90.m: and having gratified the ancestors, as he was about to offer it into the fire, / just then the fire, abandoning the entire surface of the earth,

5.90.s:
gataścādarśanaṃ sadyaḥ sarveṣāṃ kṣitivāsinām ..
citte kopaṃ samādhāya śakrasyopari bhūriśaḥ .. 22 ..
5.90.d:
गतश्चादर्शनं सद्यः सर्वेषां क्षितिवासिनाम् ..
चित्ते कोपं समाधाय शक्रस्योपरि भूरिशः .. 22 ..
5.90.m: immediately vanished from the sight of all inhabitants of the earth, / harboring great anger in his heart against Indra.

5.90.s:
etasminnaṃtare vahnau martyalokādvinirgate ..
viśeṣātpīḍitā lokā ye'vaśiṣṭā dharātale .. 23 ..
5.90.d:
एतस्मिन्नंतरे वह्नौ मर्त्यलोकाद्विनिर्गते ..
विशेषात्पीडिता लोका येऽवशिष्टा धरातले .. 23 ..
5.90.m: Meanwhile, when the fire had departed from the mortal world, / the people who remained on the surface of the earth were especially afflicted.

5.90.s:
etasminnaṃtare devā brahmaviṣṇupuraḥ sarāḥ ..
vahneranveṣaṇārthāya vabhramurdharaṇītale .. 24 ..
5.90.d:
एतस्मिन्नंतरे देवा ब्रह्मविष्णुपुरः सराः ..
वह्नेरन्वेषणार्थाय वभ्रमुर्धरणीतले .. 24 ..
5.90.m: Meanwhile, the gods, led by Brahmā and Viṣṇu, / wandered the surface of the earth in search of the fire.

5.90.s:
atha tairbhramamāṇaiśca pradṛṣṭo'bhūdgajo mahān ..
niśvasanpatito bhūmau vahnitāpaprapīḍitaḥ .. 25 ..
5.90.d:
अथ तैर्भ्रममाणैश्च प्रदृष्टोऽभूद्गजो महान् ..
निश्वसन्पतितो भूमौ वह्नितापप्रपीडितः .. 25 ..
5.90.m: Then, as they were wandering, a large elephant was seen, / sighing, fallen on the ground, afflicted by the heat of the fire.

5.90.s:
atha devā gajaṃ dṛṣṭvā papracchustvarayā'nvitāḥ ..
kaccittvayā sa dṛṣṭo'tra kānane pāvako gaja .. 26 ..
5.90.d:
अथ देवा गजं दृष्ट्वा पप्रच्छुस्त्वरयाऽन्विताः ..
कच्चित्त्वया स दृष्टोऽत्र कानने पावको गज .. 26 ..
5.90.m: Then the gods, seeing the elephant, asked with haste: / 'Was the fire seen here by you in the forest, O elephant?'

5.90.s:
.. gaja uvāca ..
vaṃśastaṃbe'tra saṃkīrṇe saṃpraviṣṭo hutāśanaḥ ..
sāṃprataṃ tena nirdagdhaḥ kṛcchrādatrāhamāgataḥ .. 27 ..
5.90.d:
.. गज उवाच ..
वंशस्तंबेऽत्र संकीर्णे संप्रविष्टो हुताशनः ..
सांप्रतं तेन निर्दग्धः कृच्छ्रादत्राहमागतः .. 27 ..
5.90.m: The elephant said: / 'The fire has entered into this dense thicket of reeds; / just now, scorched by it, I have come here with difficulty.'

5.90.s:
atha tairveṣṭitastasminvaṃśastaṃbe hutāśanaḥ ..
devairdattvā gajeṃdrasya śāpaṃ paścādvinirgataḥ .. .. 28 ..
5.90.d:
अथ तैर्वेष्टितस्तस्मिन्वंशस्तंबे हुताशनः ..
देवैर्दत्त्वा गजेंद्रस्य शापं पश्चाद्विनिर्गतः .. .. 28 ..
5.90.m: Then the fire, surrounded in that reed-thicket / by the gods, departed after giving a curse to the king of elephants:

5.90.s:
yasmāttvayāhamādiṣṭo devānāṃ vāraṇādhama ..
tasmāttava mukhe jihvā viparītā bhaviṣyati .. 29 ..
5.90.d:
यस्मात्त्वयाहमादिष्टो देवानां वारणाधम ..
तस्मात्तव मुखे जिह्वा विपरीता भविष्यति .. 29 ..
5.90.m: 'Because I was pointed out by you to the gods, O lowest of elephants, / therefore the tongue in your mouth shall be inverted.'

5.90.s:
evaṃ śaptvā gajaṃ śīghraṃ naṣṭo vaiśvānaraḥ punaḥ ..
devāścāpi tathā pṛṣṭhe saṃlagnāstaddidṛkṣayā .. 6.90.30 ..
5.90.d:
एवं शप्त्वा गजं शीघ्रं नष्टो वैश्वानरः पुनः ..
देवाश्चापि तथा पृष्ठे संलग्नास्तद्दिदृक्षया .. 6.90.30 ..
5.90.m: Having cursed the elephant thus, the fire quickly vanished again; / and the gods also followed close behind him, desiring to see him.

5.90.s:
atha dṛṣṭaḥ śukastaiśca bhramamāṇairmahāvane ..
bhobhoḥ śuka tvayā vahniryadi dṛṣṭo nivedyatām .. 31 ..
5.90.d:
अथ दृष्टः शुकस्तैश्च भ्रममाणैर्महावने ..
भोभोः शुक त्वया वह्निर्यदि दृष्टो निवेद्यताम् .. 31 ..
5.90.m: Then a parrot was seen by them as they were wandering in the great forest: / 'O parrot, if the fire has been seen by you, tell us!'

5.90.s:
śuka uvāca ..
yo'yaṃ saṃdṛśyate dūrācchamīgarbhe ca pippalaḥ ..
etasmiṃstiṣṭhate vahniraśvatthe surasattamāḥ .. 32 ..
5.90.d:
शुक उवाच ..
योऽयं संदृश्यते दूराच्छमीगर्भे च पिप्पलः ..
एतस्मिंस्तिष्ठते वह्निरश्वत्थे सुरसत्तमाः .. 32 ..
5.90.m:
The parrot said:
"That pippala tree which is seen from afar within the hollow of a śamī tree—
in that aśvattha tree fire is present, O best of the gods."

5.90.s:
atrastho yaḥ kulāyo ma āsīcchiśusamanvitaḥ ..
saṃdagdhastatpratāpena ahaṃkṛcchrādvinirgataḥ ..33..
5.90.d:
अत्रस्थो यः कुलायो म आसीच्छिशुसमन्वितः ..
संदग्धस्तत्प्रतापेन अहंकृच्छ्राद्विनिर्गतः ..33..
5.90.m:
"My nest, which was situated there together with my young ones,
was burned up by his heat; I escaped with difficulty."

5.90.s:
tacchrutvā taiḥ suraiḥ sarvaiḥ śamīgarbhaḥ sa tatkṣaṇāt ..
veṣṭitaḥ pāvako'pyāśu śukaṃ śaptvā vinirgataḥ .. 34 ..
5.90.d:
तच्छ्रुत्वा तैः सुरैः सर्वैः शमीगर्भः स तत्क्षणात् ..
वेष्टितः पावकोऽप्याशु शुकं शप्त्वा विनिर्गतः .. 34 ..
5.90.m:
Having heard that, the hollow of that śamī tree was at that very moment
surrounded by all those gods; and the fire, having cursed the parrot, quickly departed:

5.90.s:
ahaṃ yasmāttvayā pāpa devānāṃ saṃniveditaḥ ..
tasmācchuka na te vāṇī vispaṣṭā saṃbhaviṣyati .. 35 ..
5.90.d:
अहं यस्मात्त्वया पाप देवानां संनिवेदितः ..
तस्माच्छुक न ते वाणी विस्पष्टा संभविष्यति .. 35 ..
5.90.m:
"Since I have been revealed to the gods by you, sinful one,
therefore, parrot, your speech will not be distinct."

5.90.s:
evamuktvā jātavedā devādarśanavāṃchayā ..
hāṭakeśvaraje kṣetre devasya parameṣṭhinaḥ .. 36 ..
5.90.d:
एवमुक्त्वा जातवेदा देवादर्शनवांछया ..
हाटकेश्वरजे क्षेत्रे देवस्य परमेष्ठिनः .. 36 ..
5.90.m:
Having spoken thus, Jātavedas, wishing to avoid being seen by the gods,
in the sacred field born of Hāṭakeśvara, of the supreme god [Brahmā],

5.90.s:
jalāśayaṃ sugambhīraṃ pūrvottaradiksaṃsthitam ..
dṛṣṭvā tatra praviṣṭastu nibhṛtaṃ ca samāśritaḥ .. 37 ..
5.90.d:
जलाशयं सुगम्भीरं पूर्वोत्तरदिक्संस्थितम् ..
दृष्ट्वा तत्र प्रविष्टस्तु निभृतं च समाश्रितः .. 37 ..
5.90.m:
having seen a very deep body of water situated in the north-eastern direction,
entered it and took refuge there secretly.

5.90.s:
etasminnaṃtare tatra matsyakacchapadardurāḥ ..
vahnipratāpanirdagdhā dṛśyaṃte śataśo mṛtāḥ .. 38 ..
5.90.d:
एतस्मिन्नंतरे तत्र मत्स्यकच्छपदर्दुराः ..
वह्निप्रतापनिर्दग्धा दृश्यंते शतशो मृताः .. 38 ..
5.90.m:
Meanwhile, the fish, tortoises, and frogs there,
burned by the heat of the fire, were seen dead by the hundreds.

5.90.s:
atha caiko'rdhanirdagdha āyuḥśeṣeṇa darduraḥ ..
tasmājjalādviniṣkrāṃto dṛṣṭo devaiśca dūrataḥ .. 39 ..
5.90.d:
अथ चैकोऽर्धनिर्दग्ध आयुःशेषेण दर्दुरः ..
तस्माज्जलाद्विनिष्क्रांतो दृष्टो देवैश्च दूरतः .. 39 ..
5.90.m:
Then a single half-burned frog, by the remainder of his lifespan,
emerged from that water and was seen by the gods from afar.

5.90.s:
pṛṣṭaśca brūhi cedbheka tvayā dṛṣṭo hutāśanaḥ ..
tadarthamiha saṃprāptāḥ sarve devāḥ savāsavāḥ .. 6.90.40 ..
5.90.d:
पृष्टश्च ब्रूहि चेद्भेक त्वया दृष्टो हुताशनः ..
तदर्थमिह संप्राप्ताः सर्वे देवाः सवासवाः .. 6.90.40 ..
5.90.m:
And he was asked: "Tell us, frog, if the consumer of oblations has been seen by you;
for that purpose all the gods, along with Indra, have arrived here."

5.90.s:
.. bheka uvāca ..
asmiñjalāśaye vahniḥ sāṃprataṃ paryavasthitaḥ ..
tasyaite jalamadhyasthā mṛtā bhūrijalodbhavāḥ .. 41 ..
5.90.d:
.. भेक उवाच ..
अस्मिञ्जलाशये वह्निः सांप्रतं पर्यवस्थितः ..
तस्यैते जलमध्यस्था मृता भूरिजलोद्भवाः .. 41 ..

5.90.s:
asmākaṃ nidhanaṃ prāptaṃ kuṭumbaṃ surasattamāḥ ..
ahaṃ kṛcchreṇa niṣkrāṃta etasmājjalasaṃśrayāt .. 42 ..
5.90.d:
अस्माकं निधनं प्राप्तं कुटुम्बं सुरसत्तमाः ..
अहं कृच्छ्रेण निष्क्रांत एतस्माज्जलसंश्रयात् .. 42 ..
5.90.m:
"Our family has met its death, O best of gods;
I have come out with difficulty from this watery abode."

5.90.s:
tacchrutvā te surāḥ sarve sarvatastaṃ jalāśayam ..
veṣṭayitvā sthitāstatra vahnirbhekaṃ śaśāpa ha .. 43 ..
5.90.d:
तच्छ्रुत्वा ते सुराः सर्वे सर्वतस्तं जलाशयम् ..
वेष्टयित्वा स्थितास्तत्र वह्निर्भेकं शशाप ह .. 43 ..
5.90.m:
Having heard that, all those gods, having surrounded that body of water
on all sides, stood there; and the fire indeed cursed the frog:

5.90.s:
yasmādbheka tvayā mūḍha devebhyo'haṃ niveditaḥ ..
tasmāttvaṃ bhavitā nūnaṃ vijihvo'tra dharātale .. 44 ..
5.90.d:
यस्माद्भेक त्वया मूढ देवेभ्योऽहं निवेदितः ..
तस्मात्त्वं भविता नूनं विजिह्वोऽत्र धरातले .. 44 ..
5.90.m:
"Since I have been reported to the gods by you, foolish one,
therefore you shall surely become tongueless here on the surface of the earth."

5.90.s:
evamuktvā tataḥ sthānāttato vahnirvinirgataḥ ..
tāvatsa brahmaṇā proktaḥ svayameva mahātmanā .. 45 ..
5.90.d:
एवमुक्त्वा ततः स्थानात्ततो वह्निर्विनिर्गतः ..
तावत्स ब्रह्मणा प्रोक्तः स्वयमेव महात्मना .. 45 ..
5.90.m:
Having spoken thus, the fire then came out from that place.
Then he was addressed by the great-souled Brahmā himself:

5.90.s:
bhobho vahne kimarthaṃ tvaṃ devāndṛṣṭvā pragacchasi ..
tvamādyaścaiva sarveṣāmeteṣāṃ saṃsthito mukham .. 46 ..
5.90.d:
भोभो वह्ने किमर्थं त्वं देवान्दृष्ट्वा प्रगच्छसि ..
त्वमाद्यश्चैव सर्वेषामेतेषां संस्थितो मुखम् .. 46 ..
5.90.m:
"O Fire, why do you run away upon seeing the gods?
You are the foremost of all these [gods], and you are established as their mouth.

5.90.s:
tvayyāhutirhutā samyagādityamupatiṣṭhate ..
ādityājjāyate vṛṣṭirvṛṣṭerannaṃ tataḥ prajāḥ .. 47 ..
5.90.d:
त्वय्याहुतिर्हुता सम्यगादित्यमुपतिष्ठते ..
आदित्याज्जायते वृष्टिर्वृष्टेरन्नं ततः प्रजाः .. 47 ..
5.90.m:
An oblation offered properly into you approaches the sun;
from the sun rain is born, from rain comes food, and from that the creatures.

5.90.s:
tasmāddhātā vidhātā ca tvameva jagataḥ sthitaḥ ..
saṃtuṣṭe dhāryate viśvaṃ tvayi ruṣṭe vinaṃkṣyati .. 48 ..
5.90.d:
तस्माद्धाता विधाता च त्वमेव जगतः स्थितः ..
संतुष्टे धार्यते विश्वं त्वयि रुष्टे विनंक्ष्यति .. 48 ..
5.90.m:
Therefore, you alone stand as the creator and ordainer of the world;
when you are satisfied, the universe is maintained; when you are angry, it will perish.

5.90.s:
agniṣṭomādikā yajñāstvayi sarve pratiṣṭhitāḥ ..
atha sarvāṇi bhūtāni jīvaṃti tava saṃśrayāt .. 49 ..
5.90.d:
अग्निष्टोमादिका यज्ञास्त्वयि सर्वे प्रतिष्ठिताः ..
अथ सर्वाणि भूतानि जीवंति तव संश्रयात् .. 49 ..
5.90.m:
All sacrifices beginning with the Agniṣṭoma are established in you;
and all beings live by taking refuge in you.

5.90.s:
tvamagne sarvabhūtānāmantaścarasi sarvadā ..
tenaivānnaṃ ca pānaṃ ca jaṭharasthaṃ pacatyalama .. 6.90.50 ..
5.90.d:
त्वमग्ने सर्वभूतानामन्तश्चरसि सर्वदा ..
तेनैवान्नं च पानं च जठरस्थं पचत्यलम .. 6.90.50 ..
5.90.m:
O Agni, you always move inside all beings;
by that alone, [the fire] residing in the belly thoroughly digests food and drink.

5.90.s:
tasmātkuru prasādaṃ tvaṃ sarveṣāṃ ca divaukasām ..
kopasya kāraṇaṃ brūhi yatastyaktvā pragacchasi .. 51 .. ..
5.90.d:
तस्मात्कुरु प्रसादं त्वं सर्वेषां च दिवौकसाम् ..
कोपस्य कारणं ब्रूहि यतस्त्यक्त्वा प्रगच्छसि .. 51 .. ..
5.90.m:
Therefore, grant your favor to all the dwellers of heaven;
tell the reason for your anger, because of which you depart having abandoned [them]."

5.90.s:
.. sūta uvāca ..
tasya tadvacanaṃ śrutvā devasya parameṣṭhinaḥ ..
provāca praṇayātkopaṃ kṛtvā natvā ca padmajam .. 52 ..
5.90.d:
.. सूत उवाच ..
तस्य तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा देवस्य परमेष्ठिनः ..
प्रोवाच प्रणयात्कोपं कृत्वा नत्वा च पद्मजम् .. 52 ..
5.90.m:
Sūta said:
Having heard those words of that supreme god,
Agni, feeling affection rather than anger and bowing to the lotus-born [Brahmā], said:

5.90.s:
.. agniruvāca ..
ahaṃ kopaṃ samādhāya śakrasyopari padmaja ..
praṇaṣṭo jagadutsṛjya yasmāttatkāraṇaṃ śṛṇu .. 53 ..
5.90.d:
.. अग्निरुवाच ..
अहं कोपं समाधाय शक्रस्योपरि पद्मज ..
प्रणष्टो जगदुत्सृज्य यस्मात्तत्कारणं शृणु .. 53 ..
5.90.m:
Agni said:
"Conceiving anger against Indra, O lotus-born one,
I vanished, abandoning the world; hear the reason for that.

5.90.s:
anāvṛṣṭyā mahendrasya saṃjātaścauṣadhīkṣayaḥ ..
tato'smyahaṃ śvamāṃsena viśvāmitreṇa yojitaḥ .. 54 ..
5.90.d:
अनावृष्ट्या महेन्द्रस्य संजातश्चौषधीक्षयः ..
ततोऽस्म्यहं श्वमांसेन विश्वामित्रेण योजितः .. 54 ..
5.90.m:
Because of the drought caused by the great Indra, the destruction of herbs occurred;
then I was offered dog's flesh by Viśvāmitra.

5.90.s:
etasmātkāraṇānnaṣṭo na kāmānna ca saṃbhramāt ..
abhakṣyabhakṣaṇādbhītaḥ satyametanmayoditam ..55..
5.90.d:
एतस्मात्कारणान्नष्टो न कामान्न च संभ्रमात् ..
अभक्ष्यभक्षणाद्भीतः सत्यमेतन्मयोदितम् ..55..
5.90.m:
For this reason I vanished, not out of desire, nor out of confusion;
afraid of eating what is uneatable—this which I have spoken is the truth."

5.90.s:
tacchrutvā sa caturvaktraḥ śakramāha tataḥ param ..
yuktameva śikhī prāha kimarthaṃ na ca varṣasi .. 56 ..
5.90.d:
तच्छ्रुत्वा स चतुर्वक्त्रः शक्रमाह ततः परम् ..
युक्तमेव शिखी प्राह किमर्थं न च वर्षसि .. 56 ..
5.90.m:
Having heard that, the four-faced one then said to Indra:
"Fire has spoken quite appropriately; why do you not cause rain?"

5.90.s:
.. śakra uvāca ..
jyeṣṭhaṃ bhrātaramullaṃghya śaṃtanuḥ pṛthivīpatiḥ ..
pitṛpaitāmahe rājye sa niviṣṭaḥ pitāmaha .. 57 ..
5.90.d:
.. शक्र उवाच ..
ज्येष्ठं भ्रातरमुल्लंघ्य शंतनुः पृथिवीपतिः ..
पितृपैतामहे राज्ये स निविष्टः पितामह .. 57 ..
5.90.m:
Indra said:
"Bypassing his elder brother, Śaṃtanu, the ruler of the earth,
has entered upon the ancestral kingdom, O grandfather.

5.90.s:
etasmātkāraṇādvṛṣṭiḥ saṃniruddhā mayā prabho ..
tadbrūhi kiṃ karomyadya tvaṃ pramāṇaṃ pitāmaha .. 58 ..
5.90.d:
एतस्मात्कारणाद्वृष्टिः संनिरुद्धा मया प्रभो ..
तद्ब्रूहि किं करोम्यद्य त्वं प्रमाणं पितामह .. 58 ..
5.90.m:
For this reason rain has been withheld by me, O lord;
therefore tell me what I should do now; you are the authority, O grandfather."

5.90.s:
.. pitāmaha uvāca ..
tasyākramasya saṃprāptaṃ pāpaṃ tena mahībhujā ..
upabhuktamavṛṣṭyādya tasmādvṛṣṭiṃ kuru drutam .. 59 ..
5.90.d:
.. पितामह उवाच ..
तस्याक्रमस्य संप्राप्तं पापं तेन महीभुजा ..
उपभुक्तमवृष्ट्याद्य तस्माद्वृष्टिं कुरु द्रुतम् .. 59 ..
5.90.m:
The grandfather said:
"The sin incurred by that transgression has been endured
by that king by means of the drought; therefore make rain quickly,

5.90.s:
madvākyādyāti no nāśaṃ yāvadetajjagattrayam ..
akālenāpi devendra sasyābhāvādbubhukṣayā .. 6.90.60 ..
5.90.d:
मद्वाक्याद्याति नो नाशं यावदेतज्जगत्त्रयम् ..
अकालेनापि देवेन्द्र सस्याभावाद्बुभुक्षया .. 6.90.60 ..
5.90.m:
so that, by my word, these three worlds do not go to destruction
prematurely, O lord of the gods, on account of hunger due to the absence of crops."

5.90.s:
etasminnaṃtare śakra ādideśa tvarānvitaḥ ..
puṣkarāvartakānmeghānvṛṣṭyarthaṃ dharaṇītale .. 61 ..
5.90.d:
एतस्मिन्नंतरे शक्र आदिदेश त्वरान्वितः ..
पुष्करावर्तकान्मेघान्वृष्ट्यर्थं धरणीतले .. 61 ..
5.90.m:
Meanwhile, Indra, filled with haste, commanded
the Puṣkarāvartaka clouds to rain upon the surface of the earth.

5.90.s:
te'pi śakrasamādeśātsamastadharaṇītalam ..
tatkṣaṇātpūrayāmāsurgarjanto vidyudanvitāḥ .. 62 ..
5.90.d:
तेऽपि शक्रसमादेशात्समस्तधरणीतलम् ..
तत्क्षणात्पूरयामासुर्गर्जन्तो विद्युदन्विताः .. 62 ..
5.90.m:
They too, by Indra's command, filled the entire surface of the earth
at that moment, thundering and accompanied by lightning.

5.90.s:
athābravītpunarbrahmā devaiḥ sārdhaṃ hutāśanam ..
agnihotreṣu viprāṇāṃ pratyakṣo bhava pāvaka ..
sāṃprataṃ tvaṃ varaṃ mattaḥ prārthayasvābhivāṃchitam .. 63 ..
5.90.d:
अथाब्रवीत्पुनर्ब्रह्मा देवैः सार्धं हुताशनम् ..
अग्निहोत्रेषु विप्राणां प्रत्यक्षो भव पावक ..
सांप्रतं त्वं वरं मत्तः प्रार्थयस्वाभिवांछितम् .. 63 ..

5.90.s:
.. agniruvāca ..
ayaṃ jalāśayaḥ puṇyo mannāmnā pṛthivītale ..
khyātiṃ yātu caturvaktra vahnitīrthamiti smṛtam ..64..
5.90.d:
.. अग्निरुवाच ..
अयं जलाशयः पुण्यो मन्नाम्ना पृथिवीतले ..
ख्यातिं यातु चतुर्वक्त्र वह्नितीर्थमिति स्मृतम् ..64..
5.90.m:
Agni said:
"May this holy body of water become renowned on the surface of the earth
by my name, O four-faced one, remembered as Vahnitīrtha.

5.90.s:
atra yaḥ prātarutthāya snātvā śraddhā samanvitaḥ ..
agnisūktaṃ japitvā ca tvāṃ prapaśyati sādaram ..
tasya tuṣṭistvayā kāryā drutaṃ madvākyataḥ prabho .. 65 ..
5.90.d:
अत्र यः प्रातरुत्थाय स्नात्वा श्रद्धा समन्वितः ..
अग्निसूक्तं जपित्वा च त्वां प्रपश्यति सादरम् ..
तस्य तुष्टिस्त्वया कार्या द्रुतं मद्वाक्यतः प्रभो .. 65 ..
5.90.m:
Whoever, having risen in the morning, bathes here endowed with faith,
and having muttered the Agnisūkta, gazes upon you with reverence—
satisfaction must be granted to him by you quickly, according to my word, O lord."

5.90.s:
.. śrībrahmovāca ..
atra yaḥ prātarutthāya snātvā vai vedaviddvijaḥ ..
agnisūktaṃ japitvā ca vīkṣayiṣyati māṃ tataḥ .. 66 ..
5.90.d:
.. श्रीब्रह्मोवाच ..
अत्र यः प्रातरुत्थाय स्नात्वा वै वेदविद्द्विजः ..
अग्निसूक्तं जपित्वा च वीक्षयिष्यति मां ततः .. 66 ..
5.90.m:
The venerable Brahmā said:
"Whoever, having risen in the morning, bathes here, a twice-born knower of the Veda,
and having muttered the Agnisūkta, shall then gaze upon me,

5.90.s:
agniṣṭomasya yajñasya sakalaṃ lapsyate phalam ..
anekajanmajaṃ pāpaṃ nāśameṣyati pāvaka .. 67 ..
5.90.d:
अग्निष्टोमस्य यज्ञस्य सकलं लप्स्यते फलम् ..
अनेकजन्मजं पापं नाशमेष्यति पावक .. 67 ..
5.90.m:
he shall obtain the entire fruit of the Agniṣṭoma sacrifice;
and sin born of many births shall go to destruction, O purifier."

5.90.s:
.. sūta uvāca ..
evamuktvā sa bhagavānvirarāma pitāmahaḥ ..
pāvako'pi ca viprāṇāmagnihotreṣu saṃsthitaḥ .. 68 ..
5.90.d:
.. सूत उवाच ..
एवमुक्त्वा स भगवान्विरराम पितामहः ..
पावकोऽपि च विप्राणामग्निहोत्रेषु संस्थितः .. 68 ..

5.90.s:
evaṃ tatra samudbhūtaṃ vahnitīrthaṃ mahādbhutam ..
tatra snāto naraḥ prātaḥ sarvapāpaiḥ pramucyate .. 69 ..
5.90.d:
एवं तत्र समुद्भूतं वह्नितीर्थं महाद्भुतम् ..
तत्र स्नातो नरः प्रातः सर्वपापैः प्रमुच्यते .. 69 ..
5.90.m:
Thus the greatly wonderful Vahnitīrtha arose there;
a man who bathes there in the morning is freed from all sins.

5.90.s:
.. agniruvāca ..
mamātṛptasya lokeśa tāvaddvādaśavatsarān ..
kṣutpīḍāsaṃvṛte martye na prāptaṃ kutraciddhaviḥ .. 6.90.70 ..
5.90.d:
.. अग्निरुवाच ..
ममातृप्तस्य लोकेश तावद्द्वादशवत्सरान् ..
क्षुत्पीडासंवृते मर्त्ये न प्राप्तं कुत्रचिद्धविः .. 6.90.70 ..
5.90.m:
Agni said:
"For me, who have remained unsatisfied for twelve years, O lord of the world,
while mortals were afflicted by hunger, no oblation was obtained anywhere.

5.90.s:
bhaviṣyaṃti tathā yajñā kālena mahatā vibho ..
saṃjātaiḥ paśubhirbhūyaḥ sasyādairaparairbhuvi .. 71 ..
5.90.d:
भविष्यंति तथा यज्ञा कालेन महता विभो ..
संजातैः पशुभिर्भूयः सस्यादैरपरैर्भुवि .. 71 ..
5.90.m:
Sacrifices will take place only after a long time, O lord,
when animals and other crop-eating creatures have multiplied again on the earth."

5.90.s:
.. śrībrahmovāca .. ..
atra ye brāhmaṇāḥ kecinnivasaṃti hutāśana ..
vasorddhārāpradānena te tvāṃ naktaṃdinaṃ sadā .. 72 ..
5.90.d:
.. श्रीब्रह्मोवाच .. ..
अत्र ये ब्राह्मणाः केचिन्निवसंति हुताशन ..
वसोर्द्धाराप्रदानेन ते त्वां नक्तंदिनं सदा .. 72 ..
5.90.m:
The venerable Brahmā said:
"Whichever brahmins reside here, O consumer of oblations,
they, by offering the continuous flow of clarified butter, will always, day and night, [satisfy] you..."

5.90.s:
tarpayiṣyaṃti sadbhaktyā tataḥ puṣṭimavāpsyasi ..
te'pi kāmyairmano'bhīṣṭairbhaviṣyaṃti samanvitāḥ .. 73 ..
5.90.d:
तर्पयिष्यंति सद्भक्त्या ततः पुष्टिमवाप्स्यसि ..
तेऽपि काम्यैर्मनोऽभीष्टैर्भविष्यंति समन्विताः .. 73 ..
5.90.m: They will satisfy [you] with true devotion, and from that you will obtain nourishment. / They too will be endowed with their cherished desires. 73

5.90.s:
saṃkrāṃti samaye yeṣāṃ vasordhārāpradāyinām ..
bhaviṣyati kṣutaṃ vahne hūyamāne tavānala .. 74 ..
5.90.d:
संक्रांति समये येषां वसोर्धाराप्रदायिनाम् ..
भविष्यति क्षुतं वह्ने हूयमाने तवानल .. 74 ..
5.90.m: O fire, at the time of the sun's transit, when those who offer the continuous stream of clarified butter / offer oblations into you, O fire, 74

5.90.s:
teṣāṃ pāpaṃ ca yatkiṃcijjñānato'jñānataḥ kṛtam ..
tadyāsyati kṣayaṃ sarvamājanmamaraṇāṃtikam.. 75 ..
5.90.d:
तेषां पापं च यत्किंचिज्ज्ञानतोऽज्ञानतः कृतम् ..
तद्यास्यति क्षयं सर्वमाजन्ममरणांतिकम्.. 75 ..
5.90.m: whatever sin they have committed knowingly or unknowingly, / all that, from birth up to their death, will go to destruction. 75

5.90.s:
tvayi tuṣṭiṃ gate paścādbhaviṣyati mahīpatiḥ ..
śibirnāma suvikhyāta uśīnarasamudravaḥ .. 76 ..
5.90.d:
त्वयि तुष्टिं गते पश्चाद्भविष्यति महीपतिः ..
शिबिर्नाम सुविख्यात उशीनरसमुद्रवः .. 76 ..
5.90.m: When you have become satisfied, thereafter there will be a king, / highly renowned, named Śibi, born of Uśīnara. 76

5.90.s:
sa kṛtvā śraddhayā yuktaḥ satraṃ dvādaśavārṣikam..
vasorddhārāpradānena varṣaṃ tvāṃ tarpayiṣyati ..
kalaśasya ca vaktreṇāvicchinnena divāniśam .. 77 ..
5.90.d:
स कृत्वा श्रद्धया युक्तः सत्रं द्वादशवार्षिकम्..
वसोर्द्धाराप्रदानेन वर्षं त्वां तर्पयिष्यति ..
कलशस्य च वक्त्रेणाविच्छिन्नेन दिवानिशम् .. 77 ..
5.90.m: Equipped with faith, having performed a twelve-year sacrificial session, / he will satisfy you for a year with the offering of a continuous stream of clarified butter / from the mouth of a jar, uninterrupted day and night. 77

5.90.s:
tatastuṣṭiṃ parāṃ prāpya parāṃ puṣṭimavāpsyasi ..
pūjyamāno dharāpṛṣṭhe sarvairvedavidāṃ varaiḥ .. 78 ..
5.90.d:
ततस्तुष्टिं परां प्राप्य परां पुष्टिमवाप्स्यसि ..
पूज्यमानो धरापृष्ठे सर्वैर्वेदविदां वरैः .. 78 ..
5.90.m: Then, having attained supreme satisfaction, you will attain supreme nourishment, / being worshipped on the face of the earth by all the best among the knowers of the Veda. 78

5.90.s:
adyaprabhṛti yatkiṃcitkarma cātra bhaviṣyati ..
śāṃtikaṃ pauṣṭikaṃ vāpi vasorddhārāsamanvitam ..
saṃbhaviṣyati tatsarvaṃ tava tṛptikaraṃ param.. 79 ..
5.90.d:
अद्यप्रभृति यत्किंचित्कर्म चात्र भविष्यति ..
शांतिकं पौष्टिकं वापि वसोर्द्धारासमन्वितम् ..
संभविष्यति तत्सर्वं तव तृप्तिकरं परम्.. 79 ..
5.90.m: From this day forth, whatever rite there shall be here, / whether propitiatory or nourishing, accompanied by a continuous stream of clarified butter, / all that will become exceedingly satisfying to you. 79

5.90.s:
api yadvaiśvadevīyaṃ karma kiṃciddvijanmanām ..
vasorddhārāvihīnaṃ ca niṣphalaṃ saṃbhaviṣyati .. 6.90.80 ..
5.90.d:
अपि यद्वैश्वदेवीयं कर्म किंचिद्द्विजन्मनाम् ..
वसोर्द्धाराविहीनं च निष्फलं संभविष्यति .. 6.90.80 ..
5.90.m: Even whatever vaiśvadeva rite of the twice-born / is devoid of the continuous stream of clarified butter will become fruitless. 80

5.90.s:
yasmādbhavati saṃpūrṇaṃ karma yajñādikaṃ hi tat ..
śāṃtikaṃ vaiśvadevaṃ ca pūrṇāhutirihocyate .. 81 ..
5.90.d:
यस्माद्भवति संपूर्णं कर्म यज्ञादिकं हि तत् ..
शांतिकं वैश्वदेवं च पूर्णाहुतिरिहोच्यते .. 81 ..
5.90.m: Since that sacrificial rite and the like become complete through it, / [and likewise] the propitiatory and the vaiśvadeva, it is called here the full offering (pūrṇāhuti). 81

5.90.s:
yaḥ samyakchraddhayā yukto vasorddhārāṃ pradāsyati ..
sa kāmaṃ manasā dhyātaṃ samavāpsyati kṛtsnaśaḥ .. 82 ..
5.90.d:
यः सम्यक्छ्रद्धया युक्तो वसोर्द्धारां प्रदास्यति ..
स कामं मनसा ध्यातं समवाप्स्यति कृत्स्नशः .. 82 ..
5.90.m: Whoever, endowed with proper faith, offers the continuous stream of clarified butter, / he will attain completely whatever desire is meditated upon in his mind.” 82

5.90.s: iti śrīskāṃde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ ṣaṣṭhe nāgarakhaṇḍe hāṭakeśvarakṣetramāhātmye vasorddhārāmāhātmyavarṇanaṃnāma navatitamo'dhyāyaḥ .. 90 .. .. cha ..
5.90.d: इति श्रीस्कांदे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां षष्ठे नागरखण्डे हाटकेश्वरक्षेत्रमाहात्म्ये वसोर्द्धारामाहात्म्यवर्णनंनाम नवतितमोऽध्यायः .. 90 .. .. छ ..
5.90.m: Thus ends the ninetieth chapter, entitled ‘The Description of the Greatness of the Continuous Stream of Clarified Butter,’ in the Greatness of Hāṭakeśvara Sacred Field, in the Nāgarakhaṇḍa, the sixth [part] of the Skanda Mahāpurāṇa consisting of eighty-one thousand verses. 90

5.91.s:
.. sūta uvāca .. ..
evamuktvā sa bhagavānvirarāma pitāmahaḥ ..
saṃtoṣya pāvakaṃ kruddhaṃ svayameva dvijottamāḥ .. 1 ..
5.91.d:
.. सूत उवाच .. ..
एवमुक्त्वा स भगवान्विरराम पितामहः ..
संतोष्य पावकं क्रुद्धं स्वयमेव द्विजोत्तमाः .. 1 ..
5.91.m: Sūta said: / Having spoken thus, the blessed Grandfather ceased, / having Himself propitiated the enraged Fire, O best of the twice-born. 1

5.91.s:
tataḥ sarvaiḥ suraiḥ sārdhaṃ śakraviṣṇuśivādibhiḥ ..
jagāma brahmalokaṃ ca devāste ca nijaṃ padam .. 2 ..
5.91.d:
ततः सर्वैः सुरैः सार्धं शक्रविष्णुशिवादिभिः ..
जगाम ब्रह्मलोकं च देवास्ते च निजं पदम् .. 2 ..
5.91.m: Then, together with all the gods headed by Śakra, Viṣṇu, and Śiva, / he went to Brahmā's world, and those gods went to their own abodes. 2

5.91.s:
pāvako'pi dvijeṃdrāṇāmagnihotreṣu saṃsthitaḥ ..
havirjagrāha vidhivadvasorddhārodbhavaṃ tathā .. 3 ..
5.91.d:
पावकोऽपि द्विजेंद्राणामग्निहोत्रेषु संस्थितः ..
हविर्जग्राह विधिवद्वसोर्द्धारोद्भवं तथा .. 3 ..
5.91.m: Fire too, staying in the agnihotra fires of the foremost among the twice-born, / accepted according to rule the sacrificial oblation, and likewise that which arose from the continuous stream of clarified butter. 3

5.91.s:
evaṃ tatra samudbhūtamagnitīrthamanuttamam ..
yatra snāto naraḥ prātarmucyate dinajādaghāt .. 4 ..
5.91.d:
एवं तत्र समुद्भूतमग्नितीर्थमनुत्तमम् ..
यत्र स्नातो नरः प्रातर्मुच्यते दिनजादघात् .. 4 ..
5.91.m: Thus arose there the peerless Agnitīrtha, / bathing where at dawn a man is freed from the sin born of the day. 4

5.91.s:
atha saṃprasthitāndṛṣṭvā tāndevānsvāśramaṃ prati ..
gajeṃdraśukamaṇḍūkāste procurduḥkhasaṃyutāḥ ..5..
5.91.d:
अथ संप्रस्थितान्दृष्ट्वा तान्देवान्स्वाश्रमं प्रति ..
गजेंद्रशुकमण्डूकास्ते प्रोचुर्दुःखसंयुताः ..5..
5.91.m: Then, seeing those gods departing toward their own abode, / the lord of elephants, the parrot, and the frog, filled with sorrow, spoke: 5

5.91.s:
yuṣmatkṛte vayaṃ śaptāḥ pāvakena sureśvarāḥ ..
tasmājjihvākṛte'smākamupāyaściṃtyatāmapi ..6..
5.91.d:
युष्मत्कृते वयं शप्ताः पावकेन सुरेश्वराः ..
तस्माज्जिह्वाकृतेऽस्माकमुपायश्चिंत्यतामपि ..6..
5.91.m: “On your account we have been cursed by the Fire, O lords of the gods! / Therefore, let some means be devised for our tongues.” 6

5.91.s:
.. devā ūcuḥ .. ..
viparītāpi te jihvā yathānyeṣāṃ gajottama ..
kāryakṣamā na saṃdeho bhaviṣyati viśeṣataḥ .. 7 ..
5.91.d:
.. देवा ऊचुः .. ..
विपरीतापि ते जिह्वा यथान्येषां गजोत्तम ..
कार्यक्षमा न संदेहो भविष्यति विशेषतः .. 7 ..
5.91.m: The gods said: / “Although your tongue is inverted, O best of elephants, / it will be capable of its function just like those of others; of this there is no doubt. 7

5.91.s:
tathā yūyaṃ narendrāṇāṃ maṃdireṣu vyavasthitāḥ ..
bahu mānasamāyuktā mṛṣṭānnaṃ bhakṣayiṣyatha .. 8 ..
5.91.d:
तथा यूयं नरेन्द्राणां मंदिरेषु व्यवस्थिताः ..
बहु मानसमायुक्ता मृष्टान्नं भक्षयिष्यथ .. 8 ..
5.91.m: Moreover, you, staying in the palaces of kings, / accompanied by great honor, will eat sweet food. 8

5.91.s:
yathā ca śuka te jihvā kṛtā maṃdā havirbhujā ..
tathāpi bhūmipālānāṃ śaṃsanīyā bhaviṣyati .. 9 ..
5.91.d:
यथा च शुक ते जिह्वा कृता मंदा हविर्भुजा ..
तथापि भूमिपालानां शंसनीया भविष्यति .. 9 ..
5.91.m: And though your tongue, O parrot, has been made slow by the Eater of Oblations, / even so it will become praiseworthy to rulers of the earth 9

5.91.s:
śrīmatāṃ ca tathānyeṣāmasmadīyaprasādataḥ ..
tvaṃ ca maṃḍūka yattena vijihvo vahninā kṛtaḥ ..
tadbhaviṣyati te śabdo vijihvasyāpi dīrghagaḥ .. 6.91.10 ..
5.91.d:
श्रीमतां च तथान्येषामस्मदीयप्रसादतः ..
त्वं च मंडूक यत्तेन विजिह्वो वह्निना कृतः ..
तद्भविष्यति ते शब्दो विजिह्वस्यापि दीर्घगः .. 6.91.10 ..
5.91.m: and to other wealthy persons, by our grace. / And you, O frog, although you have been made tongueless by Fire, / your sound will travel far, even without a tongue.” 10

5.91.s:
evamuktvā'tha te devāḥ svasthānaṃ prasthitāstataḥ ..
teṣāmanugrahaṃ kṛtvā kṛpayā parayā yutā .. 11 ..
5.91.d:
एवमुक्त्वाऽथ ते देवाः स्वस्थानं प्रस्थितास्ततः ..
तेषामनुग्रहं कृत्वा कृपया परया युता .. 11 ..
5.91.m: Having spoken thus, those gods, filled with supreme compassion, / departed thence to their own abode after bestowing favor upon them. 11

5.91.s: iti śrīskāṃde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ ṣaṣṭhe nāgararakhaṇḍe hāṭakeśvarakṣetramāhātmye'gnitīrthotpattivarṇanaṃnāmaikanavatitamo'dhyāyaḥ .. 91 .. .. cha ..
5.91.d: इति श्रीस्कांदे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां षष्ठे नागररखण्डे हाटकेश्वरक्षेत्रमाहात्म्येऽग्नितीर्थोत्पत्तिवर्णनंनामैकनवतितमोऽध्यायः .. 91 .. .. छ ..
5.91.m: Thus ends the ninety-first chapter, entitled ‘The Description of the Origin of Agnitīrtha,’ in the Greatness of Hāṭakeśvara Sacred Field, in the Nāgarakhaṇḍa, the sixth [part] of the Skanda Mahāpurāṇa consisting of eighty-one thousand verses. 91

5.92.s:
.. sūta uvāca .. ..
agnitīrthasya māhātmyametadvaḥ parikīrtitam ..
brahmakuṃḍasamutpattiradhunā śrūyatāṃ dvijāḥ .. 1 ..
5.92.d:
.. सूत उवाच .. ..
अग्नितीर्थस्य माहात्म्यमेतद्वः परिकीर्तितम् ..
ब्रह्मकुंडसमुत्पत्तिरधुना श्रूयतां द्विजाः .. 1 ..
5.92.m: Sūta said: / “This greatness of Agnitīrtha has been proclaimed to you. / Now let the origin of Brahmakuṇḍa be heard, O twice-born! 1

5.92.s:
yadā saṃsthāpito brahmā mārkaṃḍena mahātmanā ..
tadā vinirmitaṃ tatra kuṇḍaṃ śucijalānvitam .. 2 ..
5.92.d:
यदा संस्थापितो ब्रह्मा मार्कंडेन महात्मना ..
तदा विनिर्मितं तत्र कुण्डं शुचिजलान्वितम् .. 2 ..
5.92.m: When Brahmā was installed by the great-souled Mārkaṇḍa, / a pool endowed with pure water was fashioned there at that time. 2

5.92.s:
proktaṃ ca kārtike māsi kṛttikāsthe niśākare ..
samyagbhīṣmavrataṃ kṛtvā snātvātra salile śubhe .. 3 ..
5.92.d:
प्रोक्तं च कार्तिके मासि कृत्तिकास्थे निशाकरे ..
सम्यग्भीष्मव्रतं कृत्वा स्नात्वात्र सलिले शुभे .. 3 ..
5.92.m: And it was declared: ‘In the month of Kārttika, when the moon is in Kṛttikā, / having properly performed the Bhīṣma vow and bathed here in the auspicious water, 3

5.92.s:
pūjayiṣyati yo devaṃ padmayoniṃ tataḥ param ..
sa śūdro'pi tanuṃ tyaktvā brahmayonau prayāsyati .. 4 ..
5.92.d:
पूजयिष्यति यो देवं पद्मयोनिं ततः परम् ..
स शूद्रोऽपि तनुं त्यक्त्वा ब्रह्मयोनौ प्रयास्यति .. 4 ..
5.92.m: whoever then worships the lotus-born god— / even a Śūdra, leaving his body, will go to the womb of a brahmin. 4

5.92.s:
brāhmaṇo'pi yadi snānaṃ tatra kuṇḍe kariṣyati ..
kṛtvā bhīṣmavrataṃ samyagbrahmalokaṃ prayāsyati .. 5 ..
5.92.d:
ब्राह्मणोऽपि यदि स्नानं तत्र कुण्डे करिष्यति ..
कृत्वा भीष्मव्रतं सम्यग्ब्रह्मलोकं प्रयास्यति .. 5 ..
5.92.m: Even a brahmin, if he performs a bath in that pool / after properly undertaking the Bhīṣma vow, will go to Brahmā's world.’ 5

5.92.s:
evaṃ pravadatastasya mārkaṃḍeyasya sanmuneḥ ..
śrutaṃ tatsakalaṃ vākyaṃ paśupālena kenacit .. 6 ..
5.92.d:
एवं प्रवदतस्तस्य मार्कंडेयस्य सन्मुनेः ..
श्रुतं तत्सकलं वाक्यं पशुपालेन केनचित् .. 6 ..
5.92.m: As that virtuous sage Mārkaṇḍeya was speaking thus, / all that speech was heard by a certain cowherd. 6

5.92.s:
tataḥ śraddhāprayuktena tena tadbhīṣmapaṃcakam ..
yathāvadvihitaṃ samyakkārtike māsi saṃsthite .. 7 ..
5.92.d:
ततः श्रद्धाप्रयुक्तेन तेन तद्भीष्मपंचकम् ..
यथावद्विहितं सम्यक्कार्तिके मासि संस्थिते .. 7 ..
5.92.m: Then, moved by faith, he duly performed / that five-day Bhīṣma observance when the month of Kārttika arrived. 7

5.92.s:
tataśca kṛttikāyoge pūrṇimāyāṃ yathāvidhi ..
saṃpūjya padmajaṃ paścātpūjitaḥ puruṣottamaḥ .. 8 ..
5.92.d:
ततश्च कृत्तिकायोगे पूर्णिमायां यथाविधि ..
संपूज्य पद्मजं पश्चात्पूजितः पुरुषोत्तमः .. 8 ..
5.92.m: Then, on the full moon day in conjunction with Kṛttikā, having worshipped / the lotus-born according to rule, he afterwards worshipped Puruṣottama. 8

5.92.s:
tataḥ kālavipākena sa paṃcatvamupāgataḥ ..
brāhmaṇasya gṛhe jātaḥ pure'traiva dvijottamāḥ ..
jātismaraḥ prabhāyuktaḥ pitṛmātṛpratuṣṭidaḥ .. 9 ..
5.92.d:
ततः कालविपाकेन स पंचत्वमुपागतः ..
ब्राह्मणस्य गृहे जातः पुरेऽत्रैव द्विजोत्तमाः ..
जातिस्मरः प्रभायुक्तः पितृमातृप्रतुष्टिदः .. 9 ..
5.92.m: Then, by the ripening of time, he met his death, / and was born in the house of a brahmin in this very city, O best of the twice-born, / remembering his past life, endowed with splendor, bringing delight to his father and mother. 9

5.92.s:
evaṃ pragacchatastasya vṛddhiṃ tatra purottame ..
pitṛmātṛsamudbhūto yādṛksneho vyavasthitaḥ .. 6.92.10 ..
5.92.d:
एवं प्रगच्छतस्तस्य वृद्धिं तत्र पुरोत्तमे ..
पितृमातृसमुद्भूतो यादृक्स्नेहो व्यवस्थितः .. 6.92.10 ..
5.92.m: While he was thus growing up in that excellent city, / the same kind of affection he had for his father and mother 10

5.92.s:
anyadehodbhave vāpi tasya śūdreparisthitaḥ ..
sa tasya dhanasaṃpannaḥ sadaiva kurute dvijaḥ .. 11 ..
5.92.d:
अन्यदेहोद्भवे वापि तस्य शूद्रेपरिस्थितः ..
स तस्य धनसंपन्नः सदैव कुरुते द्विजः .. 11 ..
5.92.m: he maintained also toward the Śūdra [father] born of his other body; / rich in wealth, that twice-born man continually rendered 11

5.92.s:
upakārapradānaṃ ca yatkiṃcittasya saṃmatam ..
anyasmindivase śūdraḥ sa pitā pūrvajanmanaḥ ..
tasya pañcatvamāpannaḥ saṃprāpte cāyuṣaḥ kṣaye .. 12 ..
5.92.d:
उपकारप्रदानं च यत्किंचित्तस्य संमतम् ..
अन्यस्मिन्दिवसे शूद्रः स पिता पूर्वजन्मनः ..
तस्य पञ्चत्वमापन्नः संप्राप्ते चायुषः क्षये .. 12 ..
5.92.m: benefactions and whatever was agreeable to him. / On another day, that Śūdra who had been his father in his previous life / met his death when the end of his lifespan arrived. 12

5.92.s:
atha tasya mahāśokaṃ sa kṛtvā tadanaṃtaram ..
cakāra pretakāryāṇi niḥśeṣāṇi prabhaktitaḥ .. 13 ..
5.92.d:
अथ तस्य महाशोकं स कृत्वा तदनंतरम् ..
चकार प्रेतकार्याणि निःशेषाणि प्रभक्तितः .. 13 ..
5.92.m: Then, having grieved greatly for him, he immediately thereafter / performed all the funerary rites with great devotion. 13

5.92.s:
atha tasya samālokya tādṛśaṃ tadviceṣṭitam ..
pṛṣṭaḥ sa kautukāviṣṭaiḥ pitṛmātṛsutādibhiḥ .. 14 ..
5.92.d:
अथ तस्य समालोक्य तादृशं तद्विचेष्टितम् ..
पृष्टः स कौतुकाविष्टैः पितृमातृसुतादिभिः .. 14 ..
5.92.m: Then, seeing that conduct of his, / his father, mother, sons, and others, filled with curiosity, questioned him: 14

5.92.s:
kasmāttvamasya nīcasya paśupālasya sarvadā ..
atisnehasamāyukto niḥspṛhasyāpi śaṃsa naḥ .. 15 ..
5.92.d:
कस्मात्त्वमस्य नीचस्य पशुपालस्य सर्वदा ..
अतिस्नेहसमायुक्तो निःस्पृहस्यापि शंस नः .. 15 ..
5.92.m: ‘Why are you always full of excessive affection toward this base cowherd, / who was not even related to you? Tell us! 15

5.92.s:
tasyāpi pretakāryāṇi mṛtasyāpi karoṣi kim ..
etannaḥ sarvamācakṣva na cedguhyaṃ vyavasthitam .. 16 ..
5.92.d:
तस्यापि प्रेतकार्याणि मृतस्यापि करोषि किम् ..
एतन्नः सर्वमाचक्ष्व न चेद्गुह्यं व्यवस्थितम् .. 16 ..
5.92.m: Why do you even perform the funerary rites for him now that he is dead? / Tell us all this, unless it is a secret.’ 16

5.92.s:
teṣāṃ tadvacanaṃ śrutvā kiṃcillajjāsamanvitaḥ ..
tānabravīcchṛṇudhvaṃ ca kathayiṣyāmyasaṃśayam .. 17 ..
5.92.d:
तेषां तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा किंचिल्लज्जासमन्वितः ..
तानब्रवीच्छृणुध्वं च कथयिष्याम्यसंशयम् .. 17 ..
5.92.m: Hearing their words, he, feeling somewhat ashamed, / said to them: ‘Listen, and I will tell you without a doubt.’ 17

5.92.s:
ahamasyānyadehatve putra āsaṃ susaṃmataḥ ..
paśupālanakarmajñaḥ prāṇebhyo vallabhaḥ sadā .. 18 ..
5.92.d:
अहमस्यान्यदेहत्वे पुत्र आसं सुसंमतः ..
पशुपालनकर्मज्ञः प्राणेभ्यो वल्लभः सदा .. 18 ..
5.92.m: In his other body, I was his beloved son, / skilled in the work of cattle-rearing and dearer to him than life itself.

5.92.s:
kasyacittvatha kālasya mārkaṃḍasya mahāmuneḥ ..
śrutaṃ pravadato vākyaṃ brahmakuṇḍasamudbhavam .. 19 ..
5.92.d:
कस्यचित्त्वथ कालस्य मार्कंडस्य महामुनेः ..
श्रुतं प्रवदतो वाक्यं ब्रह्मकुण्डसमुद्भवम् .. 19 ..
5.92.m: Then, after some time, words uttered by the great sage Mārkaṇḍeya / were heard concerning the origin of Brahmakuṇḍa:

5.92.s:
kārtikyāṃ kṛttikāyoge bhīṣmapañcakakṛnnaraḥ ..
samyakchraddhāsamutpanno yo'tra snānaṃ kariṣyati .. 6.92.20 ..
5.92.d:
कार्तिक्यां कृत्तिकायोगे भीष्मपञ्चककृन्नरः ..
सम्यक्छ्रद्धासमुत्पन्नो योऽत्र स्नानं करिष्यति .. 6.92.20 ..
5.92.m: “On the full moon day of Kārttika, when the moon is in Kṛttikā, a person who observes the Bhīṣmapañcaka / and, filled with perfect faith, bathes here,

5.92.s:
dṛṣṭvā pitāmahaṃ devaṃ pūjayitvā janārdanam ..
sa bhaviṣyati śūdro'pi brāhmaṇaścānyajanmani .. 21 ..
5.92.d:
दृष्ट्वा पितामहं देवं पूजयित्वा जनार्दनम् ..
स भविष्यति शूद्रोऽपि ब्राह्मणश्चान्यजन्मनि .. 21 ..
5.92.m: having seen God Pitāmaha and worshipped Janārdana, / will become a brahmin in another birth, even if he were a śūdra.”

5.92.s:
tanmayā vihitaṃ samyaksnātvā tatra śubhāvahe ..
sukuṇḍe kārtike māsi tena jāto'smi saddvijaḥ .. 22 ..
5.92.d:
तन्मया विहितं सम्यक्स्नात्वा तत्र शुभावहे ..
सुकुण्डे कार्तिके मासि तेन जातोऽस्मि सद्द्विजः .. 22 ..
5.92.m: Therefore, having duly bathed there in that auspicious, / noble pool in the month of Kārttika, I was born as a true twice-born.

5.92.s:
candrodayasya viprarṣeranvaye bhuvi viśrute ....
saṃsmaranpūrvikāṃ jāti tena sneho mama sthitaḥ ..
tasyopari mahānnityaṃ śūdrasyāpi nirargalaḥ .. 23 ..
5.92.d:
चन्द्रोदयस्य विप्रर्षेरन्वये भुवि विश्रुते ....
संस्मरन्पूर्विकां जाति तेन स्नेहो मम स्थितः ..
तस्योपरि महान्नित्यं शूद्रस्यापि निरर्गलः .. 23 ..
5.92.m: In the renowned lineage of the brahmin seer Candrodaya on earth, / remembering my former birth, great and unrestrained affection / has thus always remained in me toward him, even though he was a śūdra.

5.92.s:
ato'haṃ kṛttikāyoge kārtikyāṃ bhaktisaṃyutaḥ ..
jñātvā karomi bhīṣmasya paṃcakaṃ vratamuttamam .. 24 ..
5.92.d:
अतोऽहं कृत्तिकायोगे कार्तिक्यां भक्तिसंयुतः ..
ज्ञात्वा करोमि भीष्मस्य पंचकं व्रतमुत्तमम् .. 24 ..
5.92.m: Therefore, endowed with devotion, knowing [this], on the full moon day of Kārttika / in the conjunction with Kṛttikā, I observe the supreme vow of Bhīṣma’s five days.

5.92.s:
.. sūta uvāca .. ..
evaṃ tasya vacaḥ śrutvā te cānye ca dvijottamāḥ ...
bhīṣmasya pañcakaṃ cakruḥ samyakchraddhāsamanvitāḥ. 25 ..
5.92.d:
.. सूत उवाच .. ..
एवं तस्य वचः श्रुत्वा ते चान्ये च द्विजोत्तमाः ...
भीष्मस्य पञ्चकं चक्रुः सम्यक्छ्रद्धासमन्विताः. 25 ..
5.92.m: Sūta said: / Having heard his words, those and other foremost twice-born / observed Bhīṣma’s five days, filled with perfect faith.

5.92.s:
tataḥprabhṛti tatkuṇḍaṃ vikhyātaṃ dharaṇītale ..
sthitamuttaradigbhāge brahmakuṇḍamiti smṛtam .. 26 ..
5.92.d:
ततःप्रभृति तत्कुण्डं विख्यातं धरणीतले ..
स्थितमुत्तरदिग्भागे ब्रह्मकुण्डमिति स्मृतम् .. 26 ..
5.92.m: From then on, that pool became renowned on the surface of the earth, / situated in the northern direction and known as Brahmakuṇḍa.

5.92.s:
yaḥ snānaṃ sarvadā tatra brāhmaṇaḥ prakaroti vai ..
sa saṃbhavati vipreṃdro jāyamānaḥ punaḥ punaḥ .. 27 ..
5.92.d:
यः स्नानं सर्वदा तत्र ब्राह्मणः प्रकरोति वै ..
स संभवति विप्रेंद्रो जायमानः पुनः पुनः .. 27 ..
5.92.m: A brahmin who always bathes there / indeed becomes a prince among brahmins in birth after birth.

5.92.s: itiśrīskāṃde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ ṣaṣṭhe nāgarakhaṇḍe hāṭakeśvarakṣetramāhātmye brahmakuṇḍamāhātmyavarṇanaṃnāma dvinavatitamodhyāyaḥ ..92.. ..
5.92.d: इतिश्रीस्कांदे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां षष्ठे नागरखण्डे हाटकेश्वरक्षेत्रमाहात्म्ये ब्रह्मकुण्डमाहात्म्यवर्णनंनाम द्विनवतितमोध्यायः ..92.. ..
5.92.m: Thus ends the ninety-second chapter, titled ‘Description of the Māhātmya of Brahmakuṇḍa’, in the Māhātmya of Hāṭakeśvara Kṣetra in the Nāgarakhaṇḍa, the sixth [part] of the eighty-one-thousand-verse collection of the glorious Skanda Mahāpurāṇa.

5.93.s:
sūta uvāca .. ..
athānyadapi tatrāsti gomukhākhyaṃ suśobhanam..
yadgovaktrātpurā labdhaṃ sarvapātakanāśanam .. 1 ..
5.93.d:
सूत उवाच .. ..
अथान्यदपि तत्रास्ति गोमुखाख्यं सुशोभनम्..
यद्गोवक्त्रात्पुरा लब्धं सर्वपातकनाशनम् .. 1 ..
5.93.m: Sūta said: / Now there is another very beautiful [place] there named Gomukha, / which was obtained in ancient times from the mouth of a cow, destroying all sins.

5.93.s:
purāsīdatra gopālaḥ kaścitkuṣṭhasamāvṛtaḥ ..
camatkārapuraṃ vipra atīva kṣāmatāṃ gataḥ .. 2 ..
5.93.d:
पुरासीदत्र गोपालः कश्चित्कुष्ठसमावृतः ..
चमत्कारपुरं विप्र अतीव क्षामतां गतः .. 2 ..
5.93.m: In ancient times, O brahmins, in Camatkārapura there was a cowherd / afflicted with leprosy, who had become extremely emaciated.

5.93.s:
kasyacittvatha kālasya tena mārgeṇa gokulam ..
madhyāhnasamaye prāptaṃ caṃdre citrāsamanvitaḥ .. 3 ..
5.93.d:
कस्यचित्त्वथ कालस्य तेन मार्गेण गोकुलम् ..
मध्याह्नसमये प्राप्तं चंद्रे चित्रासमन्वितः .. 3 ..
5.93.m: Then, after some time, a herd of cows along that path / reached [the spot] at midday, when the moon was united with Citrā,

5.93.s:
ekādaśyāṃ tṛṣārttaṃ ca bhāskare vṛṣasaṃsthite ..
ekayāpi tato dhenvā tṛṇastambamatīva hi ..
nīlamālokitaṃ tatra dūrādetya praharṣitā .. 4 ..
5.93.d:
एकादश्यां तृषार्त्तं च भास्करे वृषसंस्थिते ..
एकयापि ततो धेन्वा तृणस्तम्बमतीव हि ..
नीलमालोकितं तत्र दूरादेत्य प्रहर्षिता .. 4 ..
5.93.m: on the eleventh lunar day, afflicted with thirst, when the sun stood in Taurus. / Then, a very dark-green clump of grass was seen there / by a single cow; approaching from afar, overjoyed,

5.93.s:
dantairdrutaṃ samutpāṭya yāvadākarṣati dvijāḥ ..
tāvattajjaḍamārgeṇa toyadhārā vinirgatā .. 5 ..
5.93.d:
दन्तैर्द्रुतं समुत्पाट्य यावदाकर्षति द्विजाः ..
तावत्तज्जडमार्गेण तोयधारा विनिर्गता .. 5 ..
5.93.m: as she pulled it out swiftly with her teeth, O twice-born, / just then a stream of water gushed forth through the course of its roots.

5.93.s:
athāsvādya tṛṇaṃ tasmāttṛṣārtā ca śanaiḥśanaiḥ ..
papau toyaṃ suviśrabdhā susvādu kṣīrasaṃnibham .. 6 ..
5.93.d:
अथास्वाद्य तृणं तस्मात्तृषार्ता च शनैःशनैः ..
पपौ तोयं सुविश्रब्धा सुस्वादु क्षीरसंनिभम् .. 6 ..
5.93.m: Then, having tasted the grass, afflicted with thirst, little by little, / with great confidence she drank the water, which was delicious and like milk.

5.93.s:
tasyā vegena tattoyaṃ pibantyāstatrabhūtale ..
gartā jātā suvistīrṇā salilena samāvṛtā .. 7 ..
5.93.d:
तस्या वेगेन तत्तोयं पिबन्त्यास्तत्रभूतले ..
गर्ता जाता सुविस्तीर्णा सलिलेन समावृता .. 7 ..
5.93.m: From the force of her drinking that water, on that spot of earth / a very broad pit was formed, filled with water.

5.93.s:
tato'nyāḥ śataśo gāvaḥ papustoyaṃ munirmalam ..
tṛṣārttāstaddvijaśreṣṭhāḥ pīyūṣarasasaṃnibham .. 8 ..
5.93.d:
ततोऽन्याः शतशो गावः पपुस्तोयं मुनिर्मलम् ..
तृषार्त्तास्तद्द्विजश्रेष्ठाः पीयूषरससंनिभम् .. 8 ..
5.93.m: Then hundreds of other cows drank the spotless water, / O best of twice-born; afflicted with thirst, [they drank] that which was like the nectar of immortality.

5.93.s:
yathāyathā gatā gāvastatra toyaṃ pibaṃti tāḥ ..
sā gartā vaktrasaṃsparśādvṛddhiṃ yāti tathā tathā .. 9 ..
5.93.d:
यथायथा गता गावस्तत्र तोयं पिबंति ताः ..
सा गर्ता वक्त्रसंस्पर्शाद्वृद्धिं याति तथा तथा .. 9 ..
5.93.m: The more the cows went and drank the water there, / the more that pit grew in size through the touch of their mouths.

5.93.s:
tataśca gokule kṛtsne jāte tṛṣṇāvivarjite ..
gopālo'pi tṛṣārtastu tasmiṃstoye viveśa ca .. 6.93.10 ..
5.93.d:
ततश्च गोकुले कृत्स्ने जाते तृष्णाविवर्जिते ..
गोपालोऽपि तृषार्तस्तु तस्मिंस्तोये विवेश च .. 6.93.10 ..
5.93.m: And then, when the entire herd of cows had their thirst removed, / the cowherd too, tormented by thirst, entered into that water.

5.93.s:
aṃgaṃ prakṣālya pītvāpo yāvanniṣkrāmati drutam ..
tāvatpaśyati gātraṃ svaṃ dvādaśārkasamaprabham .. 11 ..
5.93.d:
अंगं प्रक्षाल्य पीत्वापो यावन्निष्क्रामति द्रुतम् ..
तावत्पश्यति गात्रं स्वं द्वादशार्कसमप्रभम् .. 11 ..
5.93.m: Having washed his limbs and drunk the water, as soon as he came out quickly, / he saw his own body possessed of the brilliance of the twelve suns.

5.93.s:
tato vismayamāpanno gatvā svīyaṃ niketanam ..
vṛtāṃtaṃ kathayāmāsa lokānāṃ purato'khilam .. 12 ..
5.93.d:
ततो विस्मयमापन्नो गत्वा स्वीयं निकेतनम् ..
वृतांतं कथयामास लोकानां पुरतोऽखिलम् .. 12 ..
5.93.m: Then, filled with amazement, having gone to his own home, / he recounted the entire event before the people:

5.93.s:
tṛṇastambaṃ yathā dhenvā tatrotpāṭya praśaktitaḥ ..
yathā vinirgataṃ toyaṃ yathā tenāvagāhitam .. 13 ..
taddṛṣṭvā mānavāḥ sarve gatvā divyaṃ jalaṃ ca tat ..
vyādhigrastā viśeṣeṇa snānaṃ cakruḥ samāhitāḥ ...4..
5.93.d:
तृणस्तम्बं यथा धेन्वा तत्रोत्पाट्य प्रशक्तितः ..
यथा विनिर्गतं तोयं यथा तेनावगाहितम् .. 13 ..
तद्दृष्ट्वा मानवाः सर्वे गत्वा दिव्यं जलं च तत् ..
व्याधिग्रस्ता विशेषेण स्नानं चक्रुः समाहिताः ...4..
5.93.m:
how the clump of grass was forcefully uprooted there by the cow, / how the water gushed forth, and how he had bathed [in it].
Having seen that, all the people went to that celestial water; / especially those afflicted with diseases bathed attentively.

5.93.s:
bhavaṃti ca vinirmuktā rogaiḥ pāpaiśca tatkṣaṇāt..
apāpāśca punaryāṃti tatkṣaṇāttridivālayam .. 15 ..
5.93.d:
भवंति च विनिर्मुक्ता रोगैः पापैश्च तत्क्षणात्..
अपापाश्च पुनर्यांति तत्क्षणात्त्रिदिवालयम् .. 15 ..
5.93.m: And they became freed instantly from diseases and from sins; / and, free from sin, they instantly went to heaven.

5.93.s:
tataḥprabhṛti tatkhyātaṃ tīrthaṃ gomukhasaṃjñitam ..
gomukhādbhūtale jātaṃ yataścaivaṃ dvijottamāḥ .. 16 ..
5.93.d:
ततःप्रभृति तत्ख्यातं तीर्थं गोमुखसंज्ञितम् ..
गोमुखाद्भूतले जातं यतश्चैवं द्विजोत्तमाः .. 16 ..
5.93.m: From then on, that sacred ford became renowned by the name Gomukha, / since it was born on earth from the mouth of a cow, O best of twice-born.

5.93.s:
atha bhītaḥ sahasrākṣastaddṛṣṭvā svargadāyakam ..
akleśena manuṣyāṇāṃ pūrayāmāsa pāṃsubhiḥ .. 17 ..
5.93.d:
अथ भीतः सहस्राक्षस्तद्दृष्ट्वा स्वर्गदायकम् ..
अक्लेशेन मनुष्याणां पूरयामास पांसुभिः .. 17 ..
5.93.m: Then the thousand-eyed Indra, seeing that it bestowed heaven upon men / without difficulty, became frightened and filled it up with dust.

5.93.s:
.. ṛṣaya ūcuḥ .. ..
kiṃ tatkāraṇamādiṣṭaṃ yena tattādṛśaṃ jalam ..
tasmātsthānādviniṣkrāṃtaṃ sūtaputra vadasva naḥ .. 18 ..
5.93.d:
.. ऋषय ऊचुः .. ..
किं तत्कारणमादिष्टं येन तत्तादृशं जलम् ..
तस्मात्स्थानाद्विनिष्क्रांतं सूतपुत्र वदस्व नः .. 18 ..
5.93.m: The seers said: / What was declared to be the cause whereby such water / emerged from that place? Tell us, O Sūta's son!

5.93.s:
.. sūta uvāca .. ..
atra pūrvaṃ tapastaptamambarīṣeṇa bhūbhujā ..
putra śokābhibhūtena toṣito garuḍadhvajaḥ .. 19 ..
5.93.d:
.. सूत उवाच .. ..
अत्र पूर्वं तपस्तप्तमम्बरीषेण भूभुजा ..
पुत्र शोकाभिभूतेन तोषितो गरुडध्वजः .. 19 ..
5.93.m: Sūta said: / Here in ancient times, King Ambarīṣa performed austerity; / overcome with grief for his son, he propitiated [Viṣṇu] whose emblem is Garuḍa.

5.93.s:
tasya putraḥ suvikhyātaḥ suvarcā iti viśrutaḥ ..
eko babhūva vṛddhatve kathaṃciddvijasattamāḥ .. 6.93.20 ..
5.93.d:
तस्य पुत्रः सुविख्यातः सुवर्चा इति विश्रुतः ..
एको बभूव वृद्धत्वे कथंचिद्द्विजसत्तमाः .. 6.93.20 ..
5.93.m: He had a renowned son known as Suvarcas, / an only [son], born somehow in his old age, O best of twice-born.

5.93.s:
pūrvakarmavipākena sa bālo'pi ca tatsutaḥ ..
kuṣṭhavyādhisamākrāṃtaḥ pitṛmātṛsuduḥkhadaḥ .. 21 ..
5.93.d:
पूर्वकर्मविपाकेन स बालोऽपि च तत्सुतः ..
कुष्ठव्याधिसमाक्रांतः पितृमातृसुदुःखदः .. 21 ..
5.93.m: Through the ripening of his past deeds, even as a child that son of his / was afflicted with the disease of leprosy, causing great sorrow to his father and mother.

5.93.s:
atha tatkāmikaṃ kṣetraṃ sa gatvā pṛthivīpatiḥ ..
cakāra roganāśāya svaputrārthaṃ mahattapaḥ .. 22 ..
5.93.d:
अथ तत्कामिकं क्षेत्रं स गत्वा पृथिवीपतिः ..
चकार रोगनाशाय स्वपुत्रार्थं महत्तपः .. 22 ..
5.93.m: Then the lord of the earth went to that wish-granting sacred field / and performed great austerity for his son's sake to destroy the disease.

5.93.s:
tatastuṣṭiṃ gatastasya svayameva janārdanaḥ ..
pradāya darśanaṃ vākyaṃ tataḥ provāca sādaram .. 23 ..
5.93.d:
ततस्तुष्टिं गतस्तस्य स्वयमेव जनार्दनः ..
प्रदाय दर्शनं वाक्यं ततः प्रोवाच सादरम् .. 23 ..
5.93.m: Then Janārdana himself, becoming pleased with him, / granted him darśana and then spoke these words with affection:

5.93.s:
parituṣṭo'smi te vatsa tasmāccitte'bhivāṃchitam ..
prārthayasva prayacchāmi varaṃ putra na saṃśayaḥ .. 24 ..
5.93.d:
परितुष्टोऽस्मि ते वत्स तस्माच्चित्तेऽभिवांछितम् ..
प्रार्थयस्व प्रयच्छामि वरं पुत्र न संशयः .. 24 ..
5.93.m: “I am well pleased with you, dear one; therefore ask for whatever is desired in your heart! / I shall grant a boon, O son, there is no doubt.”

5.93.s:
.. rājovāca .. ..
mamāyaṃ saṃmataḥ putro grastaḥ kuṣṭhena keśava ..
bālo'pi tatkuruṣvāsya kuṣṭhavyādhiparikṣayam .. 25 ..
5.93.d:
.. राजोवाच .. ..
ममायं संमतः पुत्रो ग्रस्तः कुष्ठेन केशव ..
बालोऽपि तत्कुरुष्वास्य कुष्ठव्याधिपरिक्षयम् .. 25 ..
5.93.m: The king said: / “This beloved son of mine, O Keśava, is afflicted with leprosy / though still a child; therefore bring about the complete destruction of his leprosy!”

5.93.s:
.. śrībhagavānuvāca .. ..
eṣa āsītpurā rājā meghavāhanasaṃjñitaḥ ..
brahmaṇyaśca kṛtajñaśca sarvaśāstrārthapāragaḥ .. 26 ..
5.93.d:
.. श्रीभगवानुवाच .. ..
एष आसीत्पुरा राजा मेघवाहनसंज्ञितः ..
ब्रह्मण्यश्च कृतज्ञश्च सर्वशास्त्रार्थपारगः .. 26 ..
5.93.m: The Blessed Lord said: / “In a previous life he was a king named Meghavāhana, / devoted to brahmins, grateful, and well-versed in the meaning of all śāstras.

5.93.s:
kasyacittvatha kālasya brāhmaṇo'nena ghātitaḥ ..
aṃtaḥpure niśākāle praviṣṭo jārakarmakṛta .. 27 ..
5.93.d:
कस्यचित्त्वथ कालस्य ब्राह्मणोऽनेन घातितः ..
अंतःपुरे निशाकाले प्रविष्टो जारकर्मकृत .. 27 ..
5.93.m: Then, after some time, a brahmin was killed by him / when he entered the inner quarters at night committing adultery.

5.93.s:
atha paśyati yāvatsa prabhāte'bhyudite ravau ..
yajñopavītasaṃyuktastāvatsa dvijarūpadhṛk .. 28 ..
5.93.d:
अथ पश्यति यावत्स प्रभातेऽभ्युदिते रवौ ..
यज्ञोपवीतसंयुक्तस्तावत्स द्विजरूपधृक् .. 28 ..
5.93.m: Then, when he looked at dawn after the sun had risen, / he saw that he bore the form of a twice-born, endowed with a sacred thread.

5.93.s:
atha taṃ brāhmaṇaṃ matvā ghṛṇāviṣṭaḥ suduḥkhitaḥ ..
gatvā kāśīpurīṃ paścāttapaścakre samāhitaḥ .. 29 ..
5.93.d:
अथ तं ब्राह्मणं मत्वा घृणाविष्टः सुदुःखितः ..
गत्वा काशीपुरीं पश्चात्तपश्चक्रे समाहितः .. 29 ..
5.93.m: Then, realizing he was a brahmin, overcome with remorse and deeply distressed, / he subsequently went to the city of Kāśī and performed austerity with a focused mind.

5.93.s:
rājye putraṃ samādhāya vairāgyaṃ paramaṃ gataḥ ..
niyato niyatāhāro bhikṣānnakṛtabhojanaḥ .. 6.93.30 ..
5.93.d:
राज्ये पुत्रं समाधाय वैराग्यं परमं गतः ..
नियतो नियताहारो भिक्षान्नकृतभोजनः .. 6.93.30 ..
5.93.m: Having established his son on the throne, having attained supreme dispassion, / disciplined, of restrained diet, he ate only begged food.

5.93.s:
tataḥ kālena saṃprāpto yamasya sadanaṃ prati ..
vipāpmāpi ca cihnena yukto'yaṃ pṛthivīpatiḥ .. 31 ..
5.93.d:
ततः कालेन संप्राप्तो यमस्य सदनं प्रति ..
विपाप्मापि च चिह्नेन युक्तोऽयं पृथिवीपतिः .. 31 ..
5.93.m: Then, in the course of time, this lord of the earth went to the abode of Yama; / though free from sin, he was marked with the sign

5.93.s:
brahmaghātodbhavenaiva bālabhāve'pi saṃsthite ..
ye'tra kuṣṭhasamāyuktā dṛśyaṃte mānavā bhuvi ..
tairnūnaṃ brāhmaṇāghāto vihitaścānyajanmani .. 32 ..
5.93.d:
ब्रह्मघातोद्भवेनैव बालभावेऽपि संस्थिते ..
येऽत्र कुष्ठसमायुक्ता दृश्यंते मानवा भुवि ..
तैर्नूनं ब्राह्मणाघातो विहितश्चान्यजन्मनि .. 32 ..
5.93.m: arising from the murder of a brahmin, even while still in childhood. / Whichever men are seen afflicted with leprosy here on earth, / by them, surely, the murder of a brahmin was committed in another birth.

5.93.s:
hāṭakeśvaraje kṣetre yo gatvā śrāddhamācaret ..
pitṝṇāṃ caiva sarveṣāmanṛṇaḥ sa prajāyate .. 33 .
5.93.d:
हाटकेश्वरजे क्षेत्रे यो गत्वा श्राद्धमाचरेत् ..
पितॄणां चैव सर्वेषामनृणः स प्रजायते .. 33 .
5.93.m: Whoever goes to the sacred field born of Hāṭakeśvara and performs a śrāddha, / becomes free from debt to all his ancestors.

5.93.s:
na brāhmaṇavadhādbāhyaṃ kuṣṭhavyādhiḥ prajāyate ..
etatsatyaṃ vijānīhi vadato mama bhūpate .. 34 ..
5.93.d:
न ब्राह्मणवधाद्बाह्यं कुष्ठव्याधिः प्रजायते ..
एतत्सत्यं विजानीहि वदतो मम भूपते .. 34 ..
5.93.m: The disease of leprosy does not arise without the murder of a brahmin; / know this to be true, O king, as I speak.

5.93.s:
.. aṃbarīṣa uvāca .. ..
etadarthaṃ surādhīśa mayā tvaṃ pūjitaḥ prabho ..
prasanne tvayi deveśa nāsādhyaṃ vidyate bhuvi .. 35 ..
5.93.d:
.. अंबरीष उवाच .. ..
एतदर्थं सुराधीश मया त्वं पूजितः प्रभो ..
प्रसन्ने त्वयि देवेश नासाध्यं विद्यते भुवि .. 35 ..
5.93.m: Ambarīṣa said: / For this purpose, O ruler of the gods, you have been worshipped by me, O lord. / When you are pleased, O lord of the gods, nothing on earth is impossible.

5.93.s:
evamuktastatastena bhagavānmadhusūdanaḥ ..
pātālajāhnavītoyaṃ sa sasmāra samādhinā ..36..
5.93.d:
एवमुक्तस्ततस्तेन भगवान्मधुसूदनः ..
पातालजाह्नवीतोयं स सस्मार समाधिना ..36..
5.93.m: Thus addressed by him, the blessed Madhusūdana / remembered the water of the subterranean Gaṅgā with meditative concentration.

5.93.s:
sā dhyātā sahasā tena viṣṇunā prabhaviṣṇunā ..
kṛtvā tu vivaraṃ sūkṣmaṃ viniṣkrāṃtā'tha tatkṣaṇāt .. 37 ..
5.93.d:
सा ध्याता सहसा तेन विष्णुना प्रभविष्णुना ..
कृत्वा तु विवरं सूक्ष्मं विनिष्क्रांताऽथ तत्क्षणात् .. 37 ..
5.93.m: Meditated upon suddenly by that powerful Viṣṇu, / she made a narrow opening and immediately burst forth.

5.93.s:
tataḥ provāca vacanamaṃbarīṣaṃ caturbhujaḥ ..
nimajjatu sutaste'tra supuṇye jāhnavījale .. 38 ..
5.93.d:
ततः प्रोवाच वचनमंबरीषं चतुर्भुजः ..
निमज्जतु सुतस्तेऽत्र सुपुण्ये जाह्नवीजले .. 38 ..
5.93.m: Then the four-armed [lord] spoke these words to Ambarīṣa: / "Let your son immerse himself here in the most holy water of the Gaṅgā,

5.93.s:
yena kuṣṭhavinirmuktastatkṣaṇādeva jāyate ..
tathā brahmavadhodbhūtaiḥ pātakairupapātakaiḥ .. 39 ..
5.93.d:
येन कुष्ठविनिर्मुक्तस्तत्क्षणादेव जायते ..
तथा ब्रह्मवधोद्भूतैः पातकैरुपपातकैः .. 39 ..
5.93.m: so that he will be freed that very moment from leprosy, / as well as from the major and minor sins arising from the murder of a brahmin."

5.93.s:
etasminneva kāle tu samānīya sutaṃ nṛpaḥ ..
snāpayāmāsa tattoyaiḥ pratyakṣaṃ śārṅgadhanvanaḥ .. 6.93.40 ..
5.93.d:
एतस्मिन्नेव काले तु समानीय सुतं नृपः ..
स्नापयामास तत्तोयैः प्रत्यक्षं शार्ङ्गधन्वनः .. 6.93.40 ..
5.93.m: At that very time, having brought his son, the king / bathed him with those waters before the eyes of the wielder of the Śārṅga bow.

5.93.s:
tataḥ sa bālakaḥ sadyaḥ snātamātro dvijottamāḥ ..
kuṣṭhavyādhivinirmukto jāto bālārkasaṃnibhaḥ .. 41 ..
5.93.d:
ततः स बालकः सद्यः स्नातमात्रो द्विजोत्तमाः ..
कुष्ठव्याधिविनिर्मुक्तो जातो बालार्कसंनिभः .. 41 ..
5.93.m: Then, O best of the twice-born, as soon as he had bathed, that boy at once / became freed from the disease of leprosy, resembling the rising sun.

5.93.s:
tataḥ praṇamya taṃ devaṃ harṣeṇa mahatā'nvitaḥ ..
pitrā samaṃ jagāmātha svakīyaṃ bhavanaṃ dvijāḥ .. 42 ..
5.93.d:
ततः प्रणम्य तं देवं हर्षेण महताऽन्वितः ..
पित्रा समं जगामाथ स्वकीयं भवनं द्विजाः .. 42 ..
5.93.m: Then, bowing down to that deity, filled with great joy, / he went to his own palace together with his father, O twice-born.

5.93.s:
tasmingate mahīpāle saputre tatkṣaṇāddhariḥ ..
tadraṃdhraṃ pūrayāmāsa yathā no vetti kaścana .. 43 ..
5.93.d:
तस्मिन्गते महीपाले सपुत्रे तत्क्षणाद्धरिः ..
तद्रंध्रं पूरयामास यथा नो वेत्ति कश्चन .. 43 ..
5.93.m: When that king had gone with his son, Hari instantly / filled that opening so that no one would know of it.

5.93.s:
etasmātkāraṇātpūrvaṃ tattoyaṃ sarvapāpahṛt ..
yadgomukhena bhūyo'pi bhūtale prakaṭīkṛtam .. 44 ..
5.93.d:
एतस्मात्कारणात्पूर्वं तत्तोयं सर्वपापहृत् ..
यद्गोमुखेन भूयोऽपि भूतले प्रकटीकृतम् .. 44 ..
5.93.m: For this reason, that water which destroys all sins / was previously revealed again on earth through the cow's mouth.

5.93.s:
adyāpi tajjalasparśātsupavitro dharātale ..
yaḥ snānaṃ sūryavāreṇa kurute'rkodayaṃ prati ..
tasya nāśaṃ drutaṃ yāṃti galagaṃḍādikā iha .. 49 ..
vyādhayopi mahāraudrā dadrupāmā samudbhavāḥ ..
upasargodbhavāścaiva visphoṭakavicarcikā .. 46 ..
niṣkāmastu punarmartyo yaḥ snānaṃ tatra bhaktitaḥ ..
kurute yāti lokaṃ sa devadevasya cakriṇaḥ .. 47 ..
yasmindine samānītā sā gaṃgā tatra viṣṇunā ..
tasmindine vṛṣe sūryaḥ sthitaścitrāsu caṃdramāḥ .. 48 ..
tithiścaikādaśī caiva devadevasya śārṅgiṇaḥ ..
govaktreṇa tṛṇastaṃbaṃ yasmiṃścaiva tu vāsare ..
samākṛṣṭaṃ ca tatraiva yoga evaṃ vyavasthitaḥ .. 49 ..
5.93.d:
अद्यापि तज्जलस्पर्शात्सुपवित्रो धरातले ..
यः स्नानं सूर्यवारेण कुरुतेऽर्कोदयं प्रति ..
तस्य नाशं द्रुतं यांति गलगंडादिका इह .. 49 ..
व्याधयोपि महारौद्रा दद्रुपामा समुद्भवाः ..
उपसर्गोद्भवाश्चैव विस्फोटकविचर्चिका .. 46 ..
निष्कामस्तु पुनर्मर्त्यो यः स्नानं तत्र भक्तितः ..
कुरुते याति लोकं स देवदेवस्य चक्रिणः .. 47 ..
यस्मिन्दिने समानीता सा गंगा तत्र विष्णुना ..
तस्मिन्दिने वृषे सूर्यः स्थितश्चित्रासु चंद्रमाः .. 48 ..
तिथिश्चैकादशी चैव देवदेवस्य शार्ङ्गिणः ..
गोवक्त्रेण तृणस्तंबं यस्मिंश्चैव तु वासरे ..
समाकृष्टं च तत्रैव योग एवं व्यवस्थितः .. 49 ..
5.93.m:
Even today, rendered exceedingly pure by touching its water on the earth, / whoever performs a ritual ablution on a Sunday at sunrise, / his goiter and other [ailments] quickly perish here,
and also those terrible diseases arising from ringworm and scabies, / as well as those arising from malign influences, boils, and scab.
Moreover, a mortal who, free from desire, performs a ritual ablution there with devotion, / goes to the world of the discus-bearer, the god of gods.
On the day when that Gaṅgā was brought there by Viṣṇu, / on that day the sun stood in Taurus and the moon in Citrā,
and the lunar day was the eleventh belonging to the wielder of the Śārṅga bow, the god of gods, / on the day when the clump of grass was pulled through the cow's mouth / at that very place; such was the astrological conjunction established.

5.93.s:
tathānye'pi dine tasminyadi toyamavāpya ca ..
snānaṃ karoti sadbhaktyā tatphalaṃ so'pi cāpnuyāt .. 6.93.50 ..
5.93.d:
तथान्येऽपि दिने तस्मिन्यदि तोयमवाप्य च ..
स्नानं करोति सद्भक्त्या तत्फलं सोऽपि चाप्नुयात् .. 6.93.50 ..
5.93.m: Likewise on another day, if someone obtains that water and / performs a ritual ablution with true devotion, he too will attain that fruit.

5.93.s: iti śrīskāṃde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ ṣaṣṭhe nāgarakhaṇḍe hāṭakeśvarakṣetramāhātmye gomukhatīrthamāhātmyavarṇanaṃnāma trinavatitamo'dhyāyaḥ .. 93 .. .
5.93.d: इति श्रीस्कांदे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां षष्ठे नागरखण्डे हाटकेश्वरक्षेत्रमाहात्म्ये गोमुखतीर्थमाहात्म्यवर्णनंनाम त्रिनवतितमोऽध्यायः .. 93 .. .
5.93.m: Thus ends the ninety-third chapter, named 'Description of the Glory of the Gomukhatīrtha', in the glory of the Hāṭakeśvarakṣetra, in the Nāgarakhaṇḍa, the sixth [part] of the auspicious Skandapurāṇa, a compendium of eighty-one thousand [verses].

5.94.s:
.. sūta uvāca .. ... .
tathānyā lohayaṣṭistu tasminkṣetre'tiśobhanā ..
muktā paraśurāmeṇa bhaṃktvā nijakuṭhārakam .. 1 ..
5.94.d:
.. सूत उवाच .. ... .
तथान्या लोहयष्टिस्तु तस्मिन्क्षेत्रेऽतिशोभना ..
मुक्ता परशुरामेण भंक्त्वा निजकुठारकम् .. 1 ..
5.94.m: Sūta said: / Likewise, another very splendid iron staff in that sacred field / was left by Paraśurāma after breaking his own axe.

5.94.s:
tāṃ dṛṣṭvā mānavaḥ samyagupavāsaparāyaṇaḥ ..
mucyate hi svakātpāpāttatkṣaṇādvijasattamāḥ .. 2 ..
5.94.d:
तां दृष्ट्वा मानवः सम्यगुपवासपरायणः ..
मुच्यते हि स्वकात्पापात्तत्क्षणाद्विजसत्तमाः .. 2 ..
5.94.m: Seeing it, a man who is devoted to fasting duly / is indeed freed instantly from his own sin, O best of the twice-born.

5.94.s:
.. ṛṣaya ūcuḥ .. ..
kutaḥ paraśurāmeṇa bhaṃktvā nijakuṭhārakam ..
nirmitā lohayaṣṭiḥ sā tatrotsṛṣṭā ca sā kutaḥ ..3 ..
5.94.d:
.. ऋषय ऊचुः .. ..
कुतः परशुरामेण भंक्त्वा निजकुठारकम् ..
निर्मिता लोहयष्टिः सा तत्रोत्सृष्टा च सा कुतः ..3 ..
5.94.m: The seers said: / Why, having broken his axe, was that iron staff / fashioned by Paraśurāma, and why was it discarded there?

5.94.s:
.. sūta uvāca .. ..
yadā rāmo hradaṃ kṛtvā tarpayitvā nijānpitṝn ..
gatāmarṣo dvijendrāṇāṃ dattvā yajñe vasundharām ..4..
5.94.d:
.. सूत उवाच .. ..
यदा रामो ह्रदं कृत्वा तर्पयित्वा निजान्पितॄन् ..
गतामर्षो द्विजेन्द्राणां दत्त्वा यज्ञे वसुन्धराम् ..4..
5.94.m: Sūta said: / When Rāma, having created the pool and gratified his ancestors, / having had his anger dispelled, had given the earth to the foremost twice-born in a sacrifice,

5.94.s:
tataḥ saṃprasthito hṛṣṭo dhṛtvā manasi sāgaram ..
snānārthaṃ taṃ samādāya kuṭhāraṃ bhāskaraprabham ..5..
5.94.d:
ततः संप्रस्थितो हृष्टो धृत्वा मनसि सागरम् ..
स्नानार्थं तं समादाय कुठारं भास्करप्रभम् ..5..
5.94.m: he then set out joyfully, keeping the ocean in mind, / taking that axe radiant as the sun for the purpose of a ritual bath.

5.94.s:
tadā sa munibhiḥ proktaḥ sarvaistatkṣetravāsibhiḥ ..
vāṃchadbhistu hitaṃ tasya sadā śamaparāyaṇaiḥ .. 6 ..
5.94.d:
तदा स मुनिभिः प्रोक्तः सर्वैस्तत्क्षेत्रवासिभिः ..
वांछद्भिस्तु हितं तस्य सदा शमपरायणैः .. 6 ..
5.94.m: Then he was addressed by all the sages residing in that sacred field, / who desired his welfare and were ever devoted to peace:

5.94.s:
rāmarāma mahābhāga yaddhārayasi pāṇinā..
śastraṃ pūrṇe pratijño'pi tanna yuktaṃ bhavettava .. 7 ..
5.94.d:
रामराम महाभाग यद्धारयसि पाणिना..
शस्त्रं पूर्णे प्रतिज्ञोऽपि तन्न युक्तं भवेत्तव .. 7 ..
5.94.m: "O Rāma, Rāma, of great fortune, that you hold a weapon in your hand / even though your vow has been completed, is not proper for you.

5.94.s:
anena karasaṃsthena tava kopaḥ kathaṃcana ..
na yāsyati śarīrasthastasmādenaṃ parityaja .. 9 ..
teṣāṃ tadvacanaṃ śrutvā tato rāmaḥ kṛtāṃjaliḥ ..
provāca vinayopetaḥ prahasaṃstāndvijottamān .. 9 ..
kuṭhāraścaiva vipreṃdrā rudratejodbhavena ca ..
lohena nirmitaḥ pūrvamakṣayo viśvakarmaṇā ..6.94.....
tadahaṃ saṃparityajya kathamenaṃ dvijottamāḥ ..9 .
kṣattradharmaparo'pyevaṃ pragacchāmi digaṃtaram .. 1...
5.94.d:
अनेन करसंस्थेन तव कोपः कथंचन ..
न यास्यति शरीरस्थस्तस्मादेनं परित्यज .. 9 ..
तेषां तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा ततो रामः कृतांजलिः ..
प्रोवाच विनयोपेतः प्रहसंस्तान्द्विजोत्तमान् .. 9 ..
कुठारश्चैव विप्रेंद्रा रुद्रतेजोद्भवेन च ..
लोहेन निर्मितः पूर्वमक्षयो विश्वकर्मणा ..6.94.....
तदहं संपरित्यज्य कथमेनं द्विजोत्तमाः ..9 .
क्षत्त्रधर्मपरोऽप्येवं प्रगच्छामि दिगंतरम् .. 1...
5.94.m:
While this remains in your hand, your bodily anger / will not depart in any way; therefore, abandon it."
Hearing those words of theirs, Rāma, with folded hands, / endowed with modesty and smiling, spoke to those foremost twice-born:
"O foremost vipras, this axe was fashioned long ago by Viśvakarman / from iron that arose from the fiery energy of Rudra, and it is imperishable. / How then, having cast it away, O best of the twice-born,
though devoted to the duty of a kṣatriya, shall I proceed to another quarter?

5.94.s:
yadi cainaṃ mayā muktaṃ kuṭhāraṃ ca dvijottamāḥ ..
grahīṣyati paraḥ kaścinmama vadhyo bhaviṣyati..12..
5.94.d:
यदि चैनं मया मुक्तं कुठारं च द्विजोत्तमाः ..
ग्रहीष्यति परः कश्चिन्मम वध्यो भविष्यति..12..
5.94.m: And if this axe, cast away by me, O best of the twice-born, / should be seized by anyone else, he will be worthy of death by me.

5.94.s:
nāparādhamimaṃ śaktaḥ sor̤huṃ cāhaṃ kathaṃcana ..
api brāhmaṇamukhyasya janasyānyasya kā kathā .. 13 ..
5.94.d:
नापराधमिमं शक्तः सोर्̤हुं चाहं कथंचन ..
अपि ब्राह्मणमुख्यस्य जनस्यान्यस्य का कथा .. 13 ..
5.94.m: Nor am I able to endure this transgression in any way, / even by a foremost brahmin, let alone any other person!

5.94.s:
tathāpi nāsti te śāṃtirmukte'pyasmindvijottamāḥ ..
gṛhīte'pi ca yuṣmābhistasmādrakṣyaḥ prayatnataḥ .. 14 ..
5.94.d:
तथापि नास्ति ते शांतिर्मुक्तेऽप्यस्मिन्द्विजोत्तमाः ..
गृहीतेऽपि च युष्माभिस्तस्माद्रक्ष्यः प्रयत्नतः .. 14 ..
5.94.m: Even so, you will have no peace if it is cast away, O best of the twice-born, / and if it is taken by you, it must be guarded with effort."

5.94.s:
.. brāhmaṇā ūcuḥ .. ..
yadyevaṃ tvaṃ mahābhāga rakṣārthaṃ saṃprayacchasi ..
asmākaṃ tatra bhaṃktvāśu piṃḍaṃ kṛtvā samarpaya .. 15 ..
5.94.d:
.. ब्राह्मणा ऊचुः .. ..
यद्येवं त्वं महाभाग रक्षार्थं संप्रयच्छसि ..
अस्माकं तत्र भंक्त्वाशु पिंडं कृत्वा समर्पय .. 15 ..
5.94.m: The brahmins said: / "If, O fortunate one, you hand it over to us for safekeeping, / then quickly break it, make it into a lump, and deliver it,

5.94.s:
yena rakṣāmahe sarve paramaṃ yavamāśritāḥ ..
na ca gṛhṇāti vā kaścidgate kālāṃtare'pi ca .. 16 ..
5.94.d:
येन रक्षामहे सर्वे परमं यवमाश्रिताः ..
न च गृह्णाति वा कश्चिद्गते कालांतरेऽपि च .. 16 ..
5.94.m: so that, relying on supreme effort, we all may guard it, / and no one will take it even after a long time has passed."

5.94.s:
teṣāṃ tadvacanaṃ śrutvā rāmaḥ śastrabhṛtāṃ varaḥ ..
cakre lohamayīṃ yaṣṭiṃ taṃ bhaṃktvā sa kuṭhārakam .. 17 ..
5.94.d:
तेषां तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा रामः शस्त्रभृतां वरः ..
चक्रे लोहमयीं यष्टिं तं भंक्त्वा स कुठारकम् .. 17 ..
5.94.m: Hearing those words of theirs, Rāma, the best of weapon-bearers, / broke that axe and made an iron staff.

5.94.s:
tataḥ sa brāhmaṇeṃdrāṇāmarpayāmāsa sādaram ..
rakṣārthaṃ bhārgavaśreṣṭho vinayāvanataḥ sthitaḥ .. 18 ..
5.94.d:
ततः स ब्राह्मणेंद्राणामर्पयामास सादरम् ..
रक्षार्थं भार्गवश्रेष्ठो विनयावनतः स्थितः .. 18 ..
5.94.m: Then that best of the Bhārgavas reverently handed it over to the foremost brahmins / for safekeeping, standing bent in modesty.

5.94.s:
.. brāhmaṇā ūcuḥ .. ..
lohayaṣṭimimāṃ rāma tvatkuṭhārasamudbhavām ..
vayaṃ saṃrakṣayiṣyāmaḥ pūjayiṣyāma eva hi .. 19 ..
5.94.d:
.. ब्राह्मणा ऊचुः .. ..
लोहयष्टिमिमां राम त्वत्कुठारसमुद्भवाम् ..
वयं संरक्षयिष्यामः पूजयिष्याम एव हि .. 19 ..
5.94.m: The brahmins said: / "This iron staff produced from your axe, O Rāma, / we shall protect and indeed worship.

5.94.s:
yathā śaktimayī kīrtiḥ skandasyātra pratiṣṭhitā ..
lohayaṣṭimayī tadvattava rāma bhaviṣyati .. 6.94.20 ..
5.94.d:
यथा शक्तिमयी कीर्तिः स्कन्दस्यात्र प्रतिष्ठिता ..
लोहयष्टिमयी तद्वत्तव राम भविष्यति .. 6.94.20 ..
5.94.m: Just as the fame of Skanda consisting of his spear is established here, / even so, O Rāma, will yours consist of this iron staff."

5.94.s:
bhraṣṭarājyastu yo rājā enāmārādhayiṣyati ..
svaṃ rājyamacirātprāpya sa pratāpī bhaviṣyati .. 21 ..
5.94.d:
भ्रष्टराज्यस्तु यो राजा एनामाराधयिष्यति ..
स्वं राज्यमचिरात्प्राप्य स प्रतापी भविष्यति .. 21 ..
5.94.m:
Moreover, whatever king who has lost his kingdom propitiates it,
recovering his own kingdom before long, he will become full of majesty.

5.94.s:
vidyākṛte dvijo vā yaḥ sadaināṃ pūjayiṣyati ..
sa vidyāṃ paramāṃ prāpya sarvajñatvaṃ prapatsyate .. 22 ..
5.94.d:
विद्याकृते द्विजो वा यः सदैनां पूजयिष्यति ..
स विद्यां परमां प्राप्य सर्वज्ञत्वं प्रपत्स्यते .. 22 ..
5.94.m:
Or whatever twice-born man always worships it for the sake of learning,
having attained supreme knowledge, he will reach omniscience.

5.94.s:
aputro vā naro yo'tha nārī vā pūjayiṣyati ..
etāṃ yaṣṭiṃ tvadīyāṃ ca putravānsa bhaviṣyati .. 23 ..
5.94.d:
अपुत्रो वा नरो योऽथ नारी वा पूजयिष्यति ..
एतां यष्टिं त्वदीयां च पुत्रवान्स भविष्यति .. 23 ..
5.94.m:
Or whatever childless man, or woman, worships
this staff of yours, he or she will become possessed of children.

5.94.s:
upavāsaparo bhūtvā yaścaināṃ pūjayiṣyati ..
āśvinasyāsite pakṣe caturdaśyāṃ viśeṣataḥ .. 24 ..
sa prāpsyati sadā kāmānabhīṣṭānmanasi sthitān.. .. 24 ..
5.94.d:
उपवासपरो भूत्वा यश्चैनां पूजयिष्यति ..
आश्विनस्यासिते पक्षे चतुर्दश्यां विशेषतः .. 24 ..
स प्राप्स्यति सदा कामानभीष्टान्मनसि स्थितान्.. .. 24 ..
5.94.m:
And whoever, dedicated to fasting, worships it,
especially on the fourteenth day of the dark half of the month of Āśvina,
he will always obtain the desires dwelling in his mind.

5.94.s:
evaṃ śrutvā tato rāmasteṣāmeva dvijanmanām ..
praṇamya prayayau tūrṇaṃ samudrasadanaṃ prati .. 25 ..
5.94.d:
एवं श्रुत्वा ततो रामस्तेषामेव द्विजन्मनाम् ..
प्रणम्य प्रययौ तूर्णं समुद्रसदनं प्रति .. 25 ..
5.94.m:
Having heard this, Rāma then bowed to those very twice-born men,
and quickly went towards the abode of the ocean.

5.94.s:
te'pi viprāstatastasyāścakruḥ prāsādamuttamam ..
tatra saṃsthāya tāṃ cakrustataḥ pūjāsamāhitāḥ .. 26 ..
5.94.d:
तेऽपि विप्रास्ततस्तस्याश्चक्रुः प्रासादमुत्तमम् ..
तत्र संस्थाय तां चक्रुस्ततः पूजासमाहिताः .. 26 ..
5.94.m:
Those brahmins too then built an excellent temple for it;
having established it there, intent on worship, they thereupon performed [its rites].

5.94.s:
prāpnuvaṃti ca tatpārśvātkāmāneva hṛdi sthitān ..
sustokenā'pi kālena durlabhāstridaśairapi .. 6.94.27 ..
5.94.d:
प्राप्नुवंति च तत्पार्श्वात्कामानेव हृदि स्थितान् ..
सुस्तोकेनाऽपि कालेन दुर्लभास्त्रिदशैरपि .. 6.94.27 ..
5.94.m:
And from its presence they obtained the desires residing in their hearts,
even in a very short time, [wishes] difficult to attain even by the gods.

5.94.s: iti śrīskāṃde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ ṣaṣṭhe nāgarakhaṇḍe hāṭakeśvarakṣetramāhātmye lohayaṣṭimāhātmyavarṇanaṃ nāma caturṇavatitamo'dhyāyaḥ .. 94 ..
5.94.d: इति श्रीस्कांदे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां षष्ठे नागरखण्डे हाटकेश्वरक्षेत्रमाहात्म्ये लोहयष्टिमाहात्म्यवर्णनं नाम चतुर्णवतितमोऽध्यायः .. 94 ..
5.94.m: Thus ends the ninety-fourth chapter, named 'Description of the Glory of the Iron Staff' in the Sacred Field of Hāṭakeśvara Māhātmya of the sixth [section], the Nāgarakhaṇḍa, in the glorious Skanda Mahāpurāṇa consisting of eighty-one thousand verses.

5.95.s:
.. sūta uvāca .. ..
athānyāpi ca tatrāsti deśakāmapradā nṛṇām ..
ajāpālena bhūpena sthāpitā pāpanāśanī .. 1 ..
5.95.d:
.. सूत उवाच .. ..
अथान्यापि च तत्रास्ति देशकामप्रदा नृणाम् ..
अजापालेन भूपेन स्थापिता पापनाशनी .. 1 ..
5.95.m:
Sūta said:
Now there is also another [goddess] there who grants the desires of people of the region,
established by King Ajāpāla, destroying sins.

5.95.s:
tāṃ ca śuklacaturdaśyāmajāpāleśvarīṃ naraḥ ..
yo vai pūjayate bhaktyā dhūpapuṣpānulepanaiḥ ..
sa prāpnotīpsitānkāmāndurlabhā sarvamānavaiḥ .. 2 ..
5.95.d:
तां च शुक्लचतुर्दश्यामजापालेश्वरीं नरः ..
यो वै पूजयते भक्त्या धूपपुष्पानुलेपनैः ..
स प्राप्नोतीप्सितान्कामान्दुर्लभा सर्वमानवैः .. 2 ..
5.95.m:
And on the bright fourteenth day, whatever man worships that Ajāpāleśvarī
with devotion, by means of incense, flowers, and ointments,
he attains desired wishes that are difficult to achieve for all human beings.

5.95.s:
tasyā devyāḥ prasādena satyametanmayoditam ..
ajāpālo mahīpālaḥ purā''sītsaṃmataḥ satām .. 3 ..
5.95.d:
तस्या देव्याः प्रसादेन सत्यमेतन्मयोदितम् ..
अजापालो महीपालः पुरा'ऽसीत्संमतः सताम् .. 3 ..
5.95.m:
By the grace of that goddess—this that I have spoken is true—
long ago there was King Ajāpāla, approved by the virtuous,

5.95.s:
hitakṛtsarvalokasya yathā mātā yathā pitā ..
tena rājyaṃ samāsādya pitṛpaitāmahaṃ śubham .. 4 ..
5.95.d:
हितकृत्सर्वलोकस्य यथा माता यथा पिता ..
तेन राज्यं समासाद्य पितृपैतामहं शुभम् .. 4 ..
5.95.m:
doing good to all people, like a mother, like a father.
Having obtained the auspicious kingdom of his father and grandfather,

5.95.s:
ciṃtitaṃ manasā paścātsvayameva mahātmanā ..
mayā tatkarma kartavyaṃ yadanyairiha bhūmipaiḥ ..
na kṛtaṃ na kariṣyaṃti ye bhaviṣyantyataḥ param .. 5 ..
5.95.d:
चिंतितं मनसा पश्चात्स्वयमेव महात्मना ..
मया तत्कर्म कर्तव्यं यदन्यैरिह भूमिपैः ..
न कृतं न करिष्यंति ये भविष्यन्त्यतः परम् .. 5 ..
5.95.m:
that great-souled one later reflected in his mind by himself:
'I must perform that deed which by other rulers of the earth here
has not been done, nor will be done by those who will exist hereafter.

5.95.s:
eṣa eva paro dharmo bhūpatīnāmudāhṛtaḥ ..
yatprajāpālanaṃ śaśvattāsāṃ ca sukhasaṃsthitiḥ .. 6 ..
5.95.d:
एष एव परो धर्मो भूपतीनामुदाहृतः ..
यत्प्रजापालनं शश्वत्तासां च सुखसंस्थितिः .. 6 ..
5.95.m:
This alone has been declared the supreme duty of kings:
perpetual protection of the subjects and their happy settlement.

5.95.s:
yathāyathā karaṃ bhūpāstā māṃ gṛhṇaṃti lolupāḥ ..
tathātathā manaḥkṣobho hṛdaye saṃprajāyate .. 7 ..
5.95.d:
यथायथा करं भूपास्ता मां गृह्णंति लोलुपाः ..
तथातथा मनःक्षोभो हृदये संप्रजायते .. 7 ..
5.95.m:
As greedy kings collect taxes from them,
so perturbation of the mind arises in the heart.

5.95.s:
na kareṇa vinā bhūpā hastyaśvādibalaṃ ca yat ..
śaknuvaṃti paritrātuṃ pādātaṃ ca viśeṣataḥ .. 8 ..
5.95.d:
न करेण विना भूपा हस्त्यश्वादिबलं च यत् ..
शक्नुवंति परित्रातुं पादातं च विशेषतः .. 8 ..
5.95.m:
Without taxes, kings are not able to maintain
the force of elephants, horses, and so forth, and especially the infantry.

5.95.s:
vinā tena sa gamyaḥ syānnīcānāmapi satvaram ..
etasmātkāraṇādbhūpāḥ karaṃ gṛhṇaṃti lokataḥ .. 9 ..
5.95.d:
विना तेन स गम्यः स्यान्नीचानामपि सत्वरम् ..
एतस्मात्कारणाद्भूपाः करं गृह्णंति लोकतः .. 9 ..
5.95.m:
Without that, he would quickly become vulnerable even to the base.
For this reason kings collect taxes from the people.

5.95.s:
tasmānmayā vināpyāśu nāgaiścaiva naraistathā ..
tapaḥ śaktyā prakartavyaṃ rājyaṃ nihatakaṇṭakam .. 6.95.10 ..
5.95.d:
तस्मान्मया विनाप्याशु नागैश्चैव नरैस्तथा ..
तपः शक्त्या प्रकर्तव्यं राज्यं निहतकण्टकम् .. 6.95.10 ..
5.95.m:
Therefore, even without elephants and infantry, through the power of austerity
I must quickly render my kingdom free of thorns,

5.95.s:
karānagṛhṇatā tena lokānraṃjayatā sadā ..
anyeṣāṃ bhūmipālānāṃ viśeṣeṇa mahātmanām .. 11 ..
5.95.d:
करानगृह्णता तेन लोकान्रंजयता सदा ..
अन्येषां भूमिपालानां विशेषेण महात्मनाम् .. 11 ..
5.95.m:
not collecting taxes, constantly gladdening the people,
[distinguishing myself] from other kings, especially the great-souled ones.'

5.95.s:
evaṃ citte samādhāya vasiṣṭhaṃ munipuṃgavam ..
purodhasaṃ samāhūya tataḥ provāca sādaram .. 12 ..
5.95.d:
एवं चित्ते समाधाय वसिष्ठं मुनिपुंगवम् ..
पुरोधसं समाहूय ततः प्रोवाच सादरम् .. 12 ..
5.95.m:
Having thus determined in his mind, having summoned the royal chaplain Vasiṣṭha,
