the best of sages, he then respectfully addressed him:

5.95.s:
atra bhūmitale vipra sarveṣāṃ tīrthamuttamam ..
alpakālena santuṣṭiṃ yatra yāti maheśvaraḥ ..
vāsudevo'thavā brahmā hyetacchīghraṃ vadasva me .. 13 ..
5.95.d:
अत्र भूमितले विप्र सर्वेषां तीर्थमुत्तमम् ..
अल्पकालेन सन्तुष्टिं यत्र याति महेश्वरः ..
वासुदेवोऽथवा ब्रह्मा ह्येतच्छीघ्रं वदस्व मे .. 13 ..
5.95.m:
“O brahmin, tell me quickly, on the surface of this earth,
which is the most excellent sacred ford of all, where Maheśvara,
or Vāsudeva, or Brahmā attains satisfaction in a short time?

5.95.s:
yenāhaṃ sarvalokasya hitārthaṃ tapa ādade ..
na svārthaṃ brāhmaṇaśreṣṭha satyenātmānamālabhe .. 14 ..
5.95.d:
येनाहं सर्वलोकस्य हितार्थं तप आददे ..
न स्वार्थं ब्राह्मणश्रेष्ठ सत्येनात्मानमालभे .. 14 ..
5.95.m:
By means of which I may undertake austerity for the benefit of all people,
not for self-interest, O best of brahmins; I swear by truth by my own self.”

5.95.s:
.. vasiṣṭha uvāca ..
tisraḥ koṭyordhakoṭī ca tīrthānāmiha bhūtale ..
saṃti pārthivaśārdūla prabhāvasahitāni ca .. 15 ..
5.95.d:
.. वसिष्ठ उवाच ..
तिस्रः कोट्योर्धकोटी च तीर्थानामिह भूतले ..
संति पार्थिवशार्दूल प्रभावसहितानि च .. 15 ..
5.95.m:
Vasiṣṭha said:
“Three and a half crores of sacred fords are on this earth,
O tiger among kings, endowed with spiritual power.

5.95.s:
aṣṭaṣaṣṭistathā rājankṣetrāṇāmasti bhūtale ..
yeṣāṃ sāṃnidhyamabhyeti sarvadaiva maheśvaraḥ .. 16 ..
5.95.d:
अष्टषष्टिस्तथा राजन्क्षेत्राणामस्ति भूतले ..
येषां सांनिध्यमभ्येति सर्वदैव महेश्वरः .. 16 ..
5.95.m:
Likewise, O king, there are sixty-eight sacred fields on the surface of the earth,
to which Maheśvara always grants his presence.

5.95.s:
tathā sarve surāstuṣṭā brahmaviṣṇu śivādayaḥ ..
paraṃ siddhipradaṃ śīghraṃ mānuṣāṇāṃ mahīpate .. 17 ..
5.95.d:
तथा सर्वे सुरास्तुष्टा ब्रह्मविष्णु शिवादयः ..
परं सिद्धिप्रदं शीघ्रं मानुषाणां महीपते .. 17 ..
5.95.m:
Likewise, all the gods are pleased—Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Śiva, and the others.
Conferring supreme perfection quickly upon mortals, O king,

5.95.s:
hāṭakeśvaradevasya kṣetraṃ pātakanāśanam ..
devānāmapi sarveṣāṃ tuṣṭiṃ gacchati caṃḍikā .. 18 ..
5.95.d:
हाटकेश्वरदेवस्य क्षेत्रं पातकनाशनम् ..
देवानामपि सर्वेषां तुष्टिं गच्छति चंडिका .. 18 ..
5.95.m:
is the sacred field of the deity Hāṭakeśvara, which destroys sins.
Caṇḍikā, [worshipped] by all the gods as well, attains satisfaction

5.95.s:
śīghramārādhitā samyakchraddhāyuktairnarairbhuvi ..
tasmāttatkṣetramāsādya tāṃ devīṃ śraddhayānvitaḥ ..
ārādhaya mahābhāga drutaṃ siddhimavāpsyasi ... .. 19 ..
5.95.d:
शीघ्रमाराधिता सम्यक्छ्रद्धायुक्तैर्नरैर्भुवि ..
तस्मात्तत्क्षेत्रमासाद्य तां देवीं श्रद्धयान्वितः ..
आराधय महाभाग द्रुतं सिद्धिमवाप्स्यसि ... .. 19 ..
5.95.m:
quickly, when properly propitiated on earth by people endowed with faith.
Therefore, having reached that sacred field, endowed with faith,
propitiate that goddess, O highly fortunate one; swiftly you will obtain perfection.”

5.95.s:
evamuktaḥ sa tenātha gatvā tatkṣetramuttamam ..
pratiṣṭhāpya ca devīṃ tāṃ pūjayāmāsa bhaktitaḥ .. 6.95.20 ..
5.95.d:
एवमुक्तः स तेनाथ गत्वा तत्क्षेत्रमुत्तमम् ..
प्रतिष्ठाप्य च देवीं तां पूजयामास भक्तितः .. 6.95.20 ..
5.95.m:
Having thus been addressed by him, he then went to that excellent sacred field,
and having installed that goddess, he worshipped her with devotion,

5.95.s:
brahmacaryaparo bhūtvā śucirvrataparāyaṇaḥ ..
niyato niyatāhārastrikālaṃ snānamācaran .. 21 ..
5.95.d:
ब्रह्मचर्यपरो भूत्वा शुचिर्व्रतपरायणः ..
नियतो नियताहारस्त्रिकालं स्नानमाचरन् .. 21 ..
5.95.m:
practicing celibacy, pure, devoted to his vow,
restrained, with limited diet, performing ritual ablutions at the three junctures of the day.

5.95.s:
evamārādhyatastatra gandhapuṣpānulepanaiḥ ..
pūjāparasya sā devī tasya tuṣṭiṃ tato gatā .. 22 .. ..
5.95.d:
एवमाराध्यतस्तत्र गन्धपुष्पानुलेपनैः ..
पूजापरस्य सा देवी तस्य तुष्टिं ततो गता .. 22 .. ..
5.95.m:
As he thus propitiated her there with incense, flowers, and ointments,
intent on worship, that goddess then became pleased with him.

5.95.s:
..devyuvāca .. ..
parituṣṭāsmi te vatsa vratenānena nityathaḥ ..
balipūjāvidhānena vihitenāmunā svayam .. 23 ..
5.95.d:
..देव्युवाच .. ..
परितुष्टास्मि ते वत्स व्रतेनानेन नित्यथः ..
बलिपूजाविधानेन विहितेनामुना स्वयम् .. 23 ..
5.95.m:
The goddess said:
“I am exceedingly pleased with you, child, by this continuous vow,
by this arrangement of offerings and worship performed by yourself.

5.95.s:
tadbrūhi yena te sarvaṃ prakaromi hṛdi sthitam ..
sadya eva mahīpāla tridaśairapi durlabham .. 24 ..
5.95.d:
तद्ब्रूहि येन ते सर्वं प्रकरोमि हृदि स्थितम् ..
सद्य एव महीपाल त्रिदशैरपि दुर्लभम् .. 24 ..
5.95.m:
Therefore speak, so that I may grant all that is in your heart,
instantly, O ruler of the earth, even that which is difficult for the gods to attain.”

5.95.s:
..rājovāca .. ..
lokānāṃ hitakāmena mayaitadvratamāhṛtam ..
yena teṣāṃ bhavetsaukhyaṃ matprasādādanuttamam ..25..
5.95.d:
..राजोवाच .. ..
लोकानां हितकामेन मयैतद्व्रतमाहृतम् ..
येन तेषां भवेत्सौख्यं मत्प्रसादादनुत्तमम् ..25..
5.95.m:
The king said:
“With a desire for the welfare of the people this vow was undertaken by me,
so that through my favor peerless happiness may belong to them.

5.95.s:
tasmāddehi mahābhāge jñānayuktāni bhūriśaḥ ..
mamāstrāṇi vicitrāṇi svairagāṇi samantataḥ ..26..
5.95.d:
तस्माद्देहि महाभागे ज्ञानयुक्तानि भूरिशः ..
ममास्त्राणि विचित्राणि स्वैरगाणि समन्ततः ..26..
5.95.m:
Therefore, O highly fortunate one, grant to me manifold, wondrous weapons
endowed with consciousness, which move everywhere at will,

5.95.s:
yāni jānaṃti bhūpṛṣṭhe mama pārśve sthitānyapi ..
aparādhaṃ sadā loke paradārādi yatkṛtam 27 ..
5.95.d:
यानि जानंति भूपृष्ठे मम पार्श्वे स्थितान्यपि ..
अपराधं सदा लोके परदारादि यत्कृतम् 27 ..
5.95.m:
which, even while remaining at my side, know upon the earth's surface
transgressions constantly committed in the world, such as violation of another's wife,

5.95.s:
anurūpaṃ tatastasya pātakasya vinigraham ..
prakurvaṃti mitho yena na teṣāṃ saṃkaro bhavet ..28..
5.95.d:
अनुरूपं ततस्तस्य पातकस्य विनिग्रहम् ..
प्रकुर्वंति मिथो येन न तेषां संकरो भवेत् ..28..
5.95.m:
and subsequently execute punishment corresponding to that sin,
so that there will be no intermingling of duties among them.

5.95.s:
maṃtragrāmaṃ tathā devi mama dehi pṛthagvidham ..
nigrahaṃ vyādhisattvānāṃ yena śīghraṃ karomyaham ..29..
5.95.d:
मंत्रग्रामं तथा देवि मम देहि पृथग्विधम् ..
निग्रहं व्याधिसत्त्वानां येन शीघ्रं करोम्यहम् ..29..
5.95.m:
Likewise, O goddess, grant me the diverse collection of mantras,
by which I may quickly effect the suppression of disease-causing beings,

5.95.s:
yena syurmanujāḥ sarve mama rājye sukhānvitāḥ..
nīrogāḥ puṣṭisaṃpannā bhayaśokavivarjitāḥ .. 6.95.30 ..
5.95.d:
येन स्युर्मनुजाः सर्वे मम राज्ये सुखान्विताः..
नीरोगाः पुष्टिसंपन्ना भयशोकविवर्जिताः .. 6.95.30 ..
5.95.m:
so that all humans in my kingdom may be endowed with happiness,
free from disease, possessed of vigor, and free from fear and sorrow.

5.95.s:
nāhaṃ devi kariṣyāmi hastyaśvarathasaṃgraham..
yatasteṣāṃ bhavetpuṣṭirvittairvittaṃ karairbhavet ..
gṛhītaiḥ sarvalokānāṃ tasmāttanna mamepsitam .. 31 ..
5.95.d:
नाहं देवि करिष्यामि हस्त्यश्वरथसंग्रहम्..
यतस्तेषां भवेत्पुष्टिर्वित्तैर्वित्तं करैर्भवेत् ..
गृहीतैः सर्वलोकानां तस्मात्तन्न ममेप्सितम् .. 31 ..
5.95.m:
I shall not gather elephants, horses, and chariots, O goddess,
since their nourishment comes from wealth, and wealth comes from taxes
collected from all the people; therefore that is not desired by me.”

5.95.s:
.. śrīdevyuvāca .. ..
atyadbhutataraṃ karma tvayaitatpṛthivīpate ..
prārabdhaṃ yanna kenāpi kṛtaṃ na ca kariṣyati .. 32 ..
5.95.d:
.. श्रीदेव्युवाच .. ..
अत्यद्भुततरं कर्म त्वयैतत्पृथिवीपते ..
प्रारब्धं यन्न केनापि कृतं न च करिष्यति .. 32 ..
5.95.m:
The auspicious goddess said:
“A most extraordinary undertaking has been commenced by you, O lord of the earth,
which has not been done by anyone, nor will anyone do it.

5.95.s:
tathāpyevaṃ kariṣyāmi tava dāsyāmi kṛtsnaśaḥ ..
jñānayuktāni śastrāṇi maṃtragrāmaṃ ca tādṛśam .. 33 ..
5.95.d:
तथाप्येवं करिष्यामि तव दास्यामि कृत्स्नशः ..
ज्ञानयुक्तानि शस्त्राणि मंत्रग्रामं च तादृशम् .. 33 ..
5.95.m: "Even so, I will do this: I will give you completely / weapons endowed with consciousness and a collection of mantras of that kind,

5.95.s:
gṛhyante yena te sarve vyādhayo'pi sudāruṇāḥ ..
paraṃ sadaiva te rakṣyā manmantrairapi saṃyutāḥ .. 34 ..
5.95.d:
गृह्यन्ते येन ते सर्वे व्याधयोऽपि सुदारुणाः ..
परं सदैव ते रक्ष्या मन्मन्त्रैरपि संयुताः .. 34 ..
5.95.m: by which all those very terrible diseases are seized. / Moreover, they must always be protected by you, endowed with my mantras.

5.95.s:
yadi dṛṣṭipathāttubhyaṃ kvacidyāsyaṃti dūrataḥ ..
mānavānpīḍayiṣyaṃti cirātprāpyādhikaṃ tataḥ .. 35 ..
5.95.d:
यदि दृष्टिपथात्तुभ्यं क्वचिद्यास्यंति दूरतः ..
मानवान्पीडयिष्यंति चिरात्प्राप्याधिकं ततः .. 35 ..
5.95.m: If they ever go far away out of your range of sight, / having found more [power] after a long time, they will afflict human beings.

5.95.s:
yadā tvaṃ pṛthivīpāla svargaṃ yāsyasi bhūtalāt ..
tadātra salile sthāpyā madagre(*) yadvyavasthitam .. 36 ..
5.95.d:
यदा त्वं पृथिवीपाल स्वर्गं यास्यसि भूतलात् ..
तदात्र सलिले स्थाप्या मदग्रे(*) यद्व्यवस्थितम् .. 36 ..
5.95.m: When, O protector of the earth, you go from the earthly realm to heaven, / then whatever is situated before me must be placed here in the water.

5.95.s:
sarve maṃtrāstathā'strāṇi mamavākyādasaṃśayam ..
yena syātpūrvavatsarvo vyavahāro nṛpodbhavaḥ .. 37 ..
5.95.d:
सर्वे मंत्रास्तथाऽस्त्राणि ममवाक्यादसंशयम् ..
येन स्यात्पूर्ववत्सर्वो व्यवहारो नृपोद्भवः .. 37 ..
5.95.m: All the mantras as well as the divine weapons [will be kept safe] by my command, without doubt, / by which all customary conduct originating from kings may be as before."

5.95.s:
..sūta uvāca .. ...
bāḍhamityeva tenokte tatkṣaṇāddvijasattamāḥ ..
prādurbhūtāni divyāni tasyāstrāṇi bahūni ca .. 38 ..
5.95.d:
..सूत उवाच .. ...
बाढमित्येव तेनोक्ते तत्क्षणाद्द्विजसत्तमाः ..
प्रादुर्भूतानि दिव्यानि तस्यास्त्राणि बहूनि च .. 38 ..
5.95.m: Sūta said: / When he said, "Certainly!", instantly, O best of the twice-born, / many divine missiles of his appeared,

5.95.s:
jñānasaṃpatprayuktāni yādṛśāni mahātmanā ..
tena saṃyācitānyeva vyādhimaṃtrāstathaiva ca .. 39 ..
5.95.d:
ज्ञानसंपत्प्रयुक्तानि यादृशानि महात्मना ..
तेन संयाचितान्येव व्याधिमंत्रास्तथैव च .. 39 ..
5.95.m: endowed with the wealth of consciousness, of such a kind as were requested / by that great-souled one, and likewise the mantras for diseases,

5.95.s:
vyādhayo yaiśca gṛhyaṃte mucyaṃte svecchayā sadā ..
sukhena paripālyaṃte dṛṣṭigocarasaṃsthitāḥ .. 6.95.40 ..
5.95.d:
व्याधयो यैश्च गृह्यंते मुच्यंते स्वेच्छया सदा ..
सुखेन परिपाल्यंते दृष्टिगोचरसंस्थिताः .. 6.95.40 ..
5.95.m: by which diseases are seized and released at will at all times, / [and] situated within the range of sight, they are protected with ease.

5.95.s:
tatastaṃ sakalaṃ prāpya prasādaṃ caṃḍikodbhavam ..
tacca hastyādikaṃ sarvaṃ brāhmaṇebhyo dadau nṛpa .. 41 ..
5.95.d:
ततस्तं सकलं प्राप्य प्रसादं चंडिकोद्भवम् ..
तच्च हस्त्यादिकं सर्वं ब्राह्मणेभ्यो ददौ नृप .. 41 ..
5.95.m: Then, having obtained all that favor arisen from Caṇḍikā, / that king gave all those elephants and other things to the brahmins,

5.95.s:
ekāṃ muktvā nijāṃ bhāryāmekaṃ daśarathaṃ sutam ..
tāṃścāpi sakalānvyādhīnmaṃtraiḥ saṃyamya yatnataḥ .. 42 ..
5.95.d:
एकां मुक्त्वा निजां भार्यामेकं दशरथं सुतम् ..
तांश्चापि सकलान्व्याधीन्मंत्रैः संयम्य यत्नतः .. 42 ..
5.95.m: excepting his one wife and his one son Daśaratha. / And carefully restraining all those diseases with mantras,

5.95.s:
ajārūpānsvayaṃ paścādyaṣṭimādāya rakṣati ..
evaṃ tasya narendrasya vartamānasya bhūtale .. 43 ..
5.95.d:
अजारूपान्स्वयं पश्चाद्यष्टिमादाय रक्षति ..
एवं तस्य नरेन्द्रस्य वर्तमानस्य भूतले .. 43 ..
5.95.m: having assumed the form of goats, he himself then protected [them], taking a staff. / As that lord of men was living in this manner on the earth,

5.95.s:
gupto'pi nāparādhaḥ syātkasyacitprakaṭaḥ kutaḥ ..
pramādādyadi bhūloke kaścitpāpaṃ samācaret .. 44 ..
5.95.d:
गुप्तोऽपि नापराधः स्यात्कस्यचित्प्रकटः कुतः ..
प्रमादाद्यदि भूलोके कश्चित्पापं समाचरेत् .. 44 ..
5.95.m: there could be no offense even in secret, so how could there be an open one? / If anyone out of negligence should commit a sin in the earthly world,

5.95.s:
tadrūpo nigrahastasya tatkṣaṇādeva jāyate ..
vadhaṃ vā yadi vā baṃdhaṃ kleśaṃ cā'rātisaṃbhavam .. 45 ..
5.95.d:
तद्रूपो निग्रहस्तस्य तत्क्षणादेव जायते ..
वधं वा यदि वा बंधं क्लेशं चाऽरातिसंभवम् .. 45 ..
5.95.m: a punishment corresponding to that immediately arose for him: / whether execution, or imprisonment, or torment arising from an enemy,

5.95.s:
adṛṣṭānyapi śastrāṇi tāni kurvaṃti tatkṣaṇāt ..
anyeṣāṃ ca mahīpānāṃ rājye guptānyanekaśaḥ ..
kurvanti manujāsteṣāṃ cakre vaivasvato graham .. 46 ..
5.95.d:
अदृष्टान्यपि शस्त्राणि तानि कुर्वंति तत्क्षणात् ..
अन्येषां च महीपानां राज्ये गुप्तान्यनेकशः ..
कुर्वन्ति मनुजास्तेषां चक्रे वैवस्वतो ग्रहम् .. 46 ..

5.95.m:
Hearing that speech of his, Brahmā, the grandfather of the worlds, / looked at the face of Śiva, who was seated nearby.
Then the three-eyed one, laughing loudly, said to the four-faced one, / having heard that most marvelous report originating from Yama.
Maheśvara said: / "For a king who has set out on the path of dharma and acts righteously, / how could prevention be done in this case, and what punishment [could there be]?
Therefore, because a path has been shown by that king, / an unprecedented [path] produced by dharma, executed properly by that great-souled one,
therefore by me too, O best of the gods, an unprecedented / favor must be made for him, such that dharma is not corrupted."
Having spoken thus to the four-faced one, Śiva then said to Yama: / "Tell what remains of this king Ajāpāla's lifespan, / so that, when that time arrives, I may lead him to my own abode."

5.95.m:
Yama said: / "Five thousand years of his lifespan have passed, / and fifty-five remain; how then can I wait,
O best of the gods, for such a long time while my own abode has become empty? / Therefore, devise quickly some means for destroying that."
When Yama had spoken thus, having dismissed him to his home, / [Śiva] himself, assuming the form of a tiger, went into his presence,
where that king remained intent on protecting his subjects, / roaring again and again with a sound as deep as a thundercloud.
Beholding that tiger bearing a terrible body, those goats, / terrified, fled for refuge towards Ajāpāla.
Even while that king was striving and protecting [them], / those goats were devoured by Śaṃkara in the form of a tiger.
Then, seeing the slaughter of the goats, that ruler of the earth, / casting away the staff from his hand, seized a sharp weapon,

5.95.m:
the fierce [weapon] given to him by the pleased [goddess], resembling the hot-rayed [sun]. / That weapon and the other [weapons] given by the Goddess, Śaṃkara, / Maheśvara, gradually seized with his own mouth.
Then, in the absence of weapons, although held back quickly by his beloved [wife], / the king fought that tiger in hand-to-hand combat.
Then, from the contact with his limbs, abandoning that tiger body, / [Śiva] assumed a body smeared with ashes and adorned with the moon,
having an excellent garland of severed heads, divine, accompanied by a skull-topped club and snakes. / Seeing him, that ruler of the earth, along with his wife, then bowed down;
having offered praise, standing bowed with modesty, / bathed in tears of joy, he spoke in a voice choked with delight.
The king said: / Through ignorance, O God, blows were struck by me against you, / and insult was likewise offered; forgive all that, O all-pervading Lord! 75

5.95.m:
The Lord said: / O son, all this insult from you has been forgiven by me, / highly pleased at seeing your superhuman feat. 76
As the kingdom was ruled and the subjects were protected by you, O king, / in such a manner no other ruler of the earth has ever done, nor ever will do. 77
Therefore come with me to Pātāla, O best of earthly kings, / in this very body, together with this lawful wife of yours. 78
You must by no means remain any longer in the mortal world, / since the deed that arose from you is contrary to all the gods. 79
The king said: / I will do so, O God, after going to the great city of Ayodhyā, / establishing my son on the throne, and informing the ministers. 80
Moreover, O God, I was told formerly by the pleased goddess, / by whom a collection of mantras and various weapons were given: 81
“When you abandon the mortal world, which is so hard to leave, O wise one, / they must then all be thrown into my pool.” 82
