“Rāma, Rāma, mighty-armed one! Do not be overcome with sorrow! / Nor is it proper to give fire to him in any way.
For one endowed with knowledge of Brahman, especially a renunciant, / and for all yogins, the offering of fire is not fitting.
This kinsman of yours, O Rāma, has gone to the abode of Brahmā, / having released himself through the door of Brahman, the most renowned one.”
Then those ministers, having heard that voice from the sky, said: / “He is not to be grieved for, O great king, having attained supreme perfection. / Therefore, O lord, let Lakṣmaṇa be; go swiftly to your own abode.
Let the affairs of state be considered, and as for the funeral rites, / perform what is fitting out of affection for him, having consulted the best of brahmins.”
Rāma said: / “I will not go home now without Lakṣmaṇa; / I shall abandon my life here, just as that great-souled one did.
This son of mine, named Kuśa, approved by me, / has been given to you. If it pleases you, [consecrate him] in my kingdom.”

the son of Vāyu with his followers, accompanied by the son of Vālin, / and Kumuda, and Tāra, and other monkeys as well.
Therefore, having spoken to them as well, having respectfully consulted them all, / I will then go to the abode of the gods, having accomplished my purpose.”
Reflecting thus for a long time, and summoning the Puṣpaka [vimāna], / mounting it, he swiftly went toward the city named Kiṣkindhā.
Then those monkeys, seeing the radiance arising from the Puṣpaka, / knowing that the descendant of Raghu had arrived, went quickly to meet him.
Then, having bowed down from afar, falling on their knees to the ground, / uttering the cry ‘Victory!’ repeatedly on every side,
accompanied by him, they entered that great city of Kiṣkindhā, / which was decorated all around with splendid banners. / Then, descending from the excellent aerial chariot, Rāma quickly entered / into Sugrīva’s auspicious abode, which was well-adorned on all sides.

Seeing Rāma seated there and rested, the monkeys, / having worshipped him with guest-water and other offerings, then asked:
The monkeys said: / “You appear bereft of your splendor, O delight of the Raghus; / you are very emaciated and agitated. Is all well in your house?
Likewise your younger brother Lakṣmaṇa, who constantly follows [you like your own] body, / is not seen standing beside you today; why is this, descendant of Raghu?
Likewise, your beloved Sītā, who is dear to you as life, O lord— / why is she not seen by your side? This is a great wonder to us.”
Sūta said: / Hearing their words, Rāghava sighed deeply for a long time; / his eyes filled with tears, and he related everything to them.
“Then Sītā was abandoned, and likewise my brother Lakṣmaṇa; / [and] the reason for which he went there of his own accord, O best of brahmins.”
Hearing that, all the monkeys, headed by Sugrīva, / wept, sorely tormented by sorrow, and then embraced him.

5.100.m:
Having lamented aloud for a long time in this way, they then said to the best of the Raghus: / “Let an order be given, O king, that can be accomplished by us here.
Blessed are we upon the surface of the earth, to whose home you, / O best of the Raghus, come endowed with such affection.”
Rāma said: / “Having stayed for one night in your abode, O Sugrīva, / I will go in the morning to Laṅkā, where that Vibhīṣaṇa resides.
Together with your chief ministers, you too, O best of monkeys, / must come with me to the house of Vibhīṣaṇa.”
Thus ends the hundredth chapter, titled ‘Description of the Departure of Śrī Rāma to the City of Sugrīva after the Nirvāṇa of Lakṣmaṇa,’ in the context of the installation of Śrī Rāmeśvara, in the Māhātmya of Hāṭakeśvara Sacred Field, in the sixth Nāgarakhaṇḍa, in the Skanda Mahāpurāṇa of eighty-one thousand verses.

विभीषणगृहं प्राप्य तत्र सिंहासने शुभे ..
निविष्टो वानरैस्तैश्च समन्तात्परिवारितः .. 6.101.10 ..
5.101.m: Reaching the palace of Vibhīṣaṇa, he sat down there upon an auspicious lion-throne, / surrounded on all sides by those monkeys.

5.101.s:
tato nivedayāmāsa tasmai sarvaṃ vibhīṣaṇaḥ ..
rājyaṃ putrakalatrādi yaccānyadapi kiṃcana .. 11 ..
5.101.d:
ततो निवेदयामास तस्मै सर्वं विभीषणः ..
राज्यं पुत्रकलत्रादि यच्चान्यदपि किंचन .. 11 ..
5.101.m: Then Vibhīṣaṇa presented everything to him: / his kingdom, sons, wife, and whatever else [he possessed].

5.101.s:
tataḥ provāca vinayātkṛtāṃjalipuṭaḥ sthitaḥ ..
ādeśo dīyatāṃ deva brūhi kṛtyaṃ karomi kim .. 12 ..
akasmādeva saṃprāptaḥ kimarthaṃ vada me prabho ..
kiṃ nāyātaḥ sa saumitristvayā sārdha ca jānakī ...3..
5.101.d:
ततः प्रोवाच विनयात्कृतांजलिपुटः स्थितः ..
आदेशो दीयतां देव ब्रूहि कृत्यं करोमि किम् .. 12 ..
अकस्मादेव संप्राप्तः किमर्थं वद मे प्रभो ..
किं नायातः स सौमित्रिस्त्वया सार्ध च जानकी ...3..
5.101.m:
Then, standing with folded hands, he said out of humility: / “Let a command be given, O Lord! Tell me what duty I shall perform.
Why have you arrived all of a sudden? Tell me, O Lord. / Why has that son of Sumitrā not come with you, nor Jānakī?”

5.101.s:
.. sūta uvāca .. ..
nivedya rāghavastasmai sarvaṃ gadgadayā girā ..
vāṣpapūrapraticchannavaktro bhūyo viniḥśvasan .. 14 ..
5.101.d:
.. सूत उवाच .. ..
निवेद्य राघवस्तस्मै सर्वं गद्गदया गिरा ..
वाष्पपूरप्रतिच्छन्नवक्त्रो भूयो विनिःश्वसन् .. 14 ..
5.101.m: Sūta said: / Having related everything to him in a choked voice, / his face covered with a flood of tears, sighing again and again,

5.101.s:
tataḥ provāca satyārthaṃ vibhīṣaṇakṛte hitam ..
taṃ cāpi śokasaṃtaptaṃ saṃbodhya raghunaṃdanaḥ .. 15 ..
5.101.d:
ततः प्रोवाच सत्यार्थं विभीषणकृते हितम् ..
तं चापि शोकसंतप्तं संबोध्य रघुनंदनः .. 15 ..
5.101.m: the joy of the Raghus then spoke truth beneficial to Vibhīṣaṇa, / comforting him who was also tormented by grief:

5.101.s:
ahaṃ rājyaṃ parityajya sāṃprataṃ rākṣasottama ..
yāsyāmi tridivaṃ tūrṇaṃ lakṣmaṇo yatra saṃsthitaḥ .. .. 16 ..
5.101.d:
अहं राज्यं परित्यज्य सांप्रतं राक्षसोत्तम ..
यास्यामि त्रिदिवं तूर्णं लक्ष्मणो यत्र संस्थितः .. .. 16 ..
5.101.m: “Having renounced the kingdom now, O best of Rākṣasas, / I shall swiftly go to heaven, where Lakṣmaṇa is residing.

5.101.s:
na tena rahito martye muhūrtamapi cotsahe ..
sthātuṃ rākṣasaśārdūla bāṃdhavena mahātmanā .. 17 ..
5.101.d:
न तेन रहितो मर्त्ये मुहूर्तमपि चोत्सहे ..
स्थातुं राक्षसशार्दूल बांधवेन महात्मना .. 17 ..
5.101.m: Bereft of him, my great-souled kin, I have no desire / to stay in the mortal world for even a moment, O tiger among Rākṣasas.

5.101.s:
ahaṃ śikṣāpaṇārthāya tava prāpto vibhīṣaṇa ..
tasmādavyagracittena saṃśṛṇuṣva kuruṣva ca .. 18 ..
5.101.d:
अहं शिक्षापणार्थाय तव प्राप्तो विभीषण ..
तस्मादव्यग्रचित्तेन संशृणुष्व कुरुष्व च .. 18 ..
5.101.m: I have come to you, Vibhīṣaṇa, to impart instruction; / therefore listen attentively and carry it out.

5.101.s:
eṣā rājyodbhavā lakṣmīrmadaṃ saṃjanayennṛṇām ..
madyavatsvalpabuddhīnāṃ tasmātkāryo na sa tvayā .. 19 ..
5.101.d:
एषा राज्योद्भवा लक्ष्मीर्मदं संजनयेन्नृणाम् ..
मद्यवत्स्वल्पबुद्धीनां तस्मात्कार्यो न स त्वया .. 19 ..
5.101.m: This fortune arising from kingship engenders intoxication in men / of small intellect, like liquor; therefore you must not indulge in it.

5.101.s:
śakrādyā amarāḥ sarve tvayā pūjyāḥ sadaiva hi ..
mānyāśca yena te rājyaṃ jāyate śāśvataṃ sadā . 6.101.20 ..
5.101.d:
शक्राद्या अमराः सर्वे त्वया पूज्याः सदैव हि ..
मान्याश्च येन ते राज्यं जायते शाश्वतं सदा . 6.101.20 ..
5.101.m: All the immortals, headed by Śakra, must always be worshipped by you, / and revered, so that your rule becomes ever permanent.

5.101.s:
mama satyaṃ bhavedvākya metasmādahamāgataḥ ..
prāptarājyapratiṣṭho'pi tava bhrātā mahābalaḥ .. 21 ..
5.101.d:
मम सत्यं भवेद्वाक्य मेतस्मादहमागतः ..
प्राप्तराज्यप्रतिष्ठोऽपि तव भ्राता महाबलः .. 21 ..
5.101.m: May my word be true; it is for this that I have come. / Even though he had obtained the sovereignty of the kingdom, your mighty brother

5.101.s:
vināśaṃ sahasā prāptastasmānmānyāḥ surāḥ sadā ..
yadi kaścitsamāyāti mānuṣo'tra kathaṃcana ..
matkāya eva draṣṭavyaḥ sarvaireva niśācaraiḥ .. 22 ..
5.101.d:
विनाशं सहसा प्राप्तस्तस्मान्मान्याः सुराः सदा ..
यदि कश्चित्समायाति मानुषोऽत्र कथंचन ..
मत्काय एव द्रष्टव्यः सर्वैरेव निशाचरैः .. 22 ..
5.101.m: suddenly met his destruction; therefore the gods must always be revered. / If any human being should happen to arrive here by any means, / all the night-wanderers must look upon him as my very own body.

5.101.s:
tathā niśācarāḥ sarve tvayā vāryā vibhīṣaṇa ..
mama setuṃ samullaṃghya na gaṃtavyaṃ dharātale .. 23 ..
5.101.d:
तथा निशाचराः सर्वे त्वया वार्या विभीषण ..
मम सेतुं समुल्लंघ्य न गंतव्यं धरातले .. 23 ..
5.101.m: Likewise, all night-wanderers must be restrained by you, Vibhīṣaṇa: / they must not cross over my bridge to go onto the earth’s surface.”

5.101.s:
.. vibhīṣaṇa uvāca .. ..
evaṃ vibho kariṣyāmi tavādeśamasaṃśayam ..
paraṃ tvayā parityakte martye me jīvitaṃ vrajet .. 24 ..
5.101.d:
.. विभीषण उवाच .. ..
एवं विभो करिष्यामि तवादेशमसंशयम् ..
परं त्वया परित्यक्ते मर्त्ये मे जीवितं व्रजेत् .. 24 ..
5.101.m: Vibhīṣaṇa said: / “Thus, O Lord, I will carry out your command without a doubt. / But once you have abandoned the mortal realm, my life will depart.

5.101.s:
tasmānmāmapi tatraiva tvaṃ vibho netumarhasi ..
ātmanā saha yatrāste prāggato lakṣmaṇastava .. 25 ..
5.101.d:
तस्मान्मामपि तत्रैव त्वं विभो नेतुमर्हसि ..
आत्मना सह यत्रास्ते प्राग्गतो लक्ष्मणस्तव .. 25 ..
5.101.m: Therefore, O Lord, you ought to take me also there, / along with yourself, where your Lakṣmaṇa has already gone.”

5.101.s:
.. śrīrāma uvāca .. ..
mayā te'kṣayamādiṣṭaṃ rājyaṃ rākṣasasattama ..
tasmānnārhasi māṃ kartuṃ mithyācāraṃ kathaṃcana .. 26 ..
5.101.d:
.. श्रीराम उवाच .. ..
मया तेऽक्षयमादिष्टं राज्यं राक्षससत्तम ..
तस्मान्नार्हसि मां कर्तुं मिथ्याचारं कथंचन .. 26 ..
5.101.m: Śrī Rāma said: / “Imperishable kingship has been ordained for you by me, O best of Rākṣasas; / therefore you ought not to make me a speaker of falsehood by any means.

5.101.s:
ahamasminsvake setau śaṃkaratritayaṃ śubham ..
sthāpayiṣyāmi kīrtyarthaṃ tatpūjyaṃ bhavatā sadā ..
bhaktimānpratisaṃdhāya yāvaccaṃdrārkatārakam .. 27 ..
5.101.d:
अहमस्मिन्स्वके सेतौ शंकरत्रितयं शुभम् ..
स्थापयिष्यामि कीर्त्यर्थं तत्पूज्यं भवता सदा ..
भक्तिमान्प्रतिसंधाय यावच्चंद्रार्कतारकम् .. 27 ..
5.101.m: Upon this bridge of mine I will establish an auspicious triad of Śaṃkara / for the sake of fame; it must always be worshipped by you, / offering [worship] with devotion as long as the moon, sun, and stars endure.”

5.101.s:
evamuktvā raghuśreṣṭho rākṣasendraṃ vibhīṣaṇam ..
daśarātraṃ tatra tasthau laṃkāyāṃ vānaraiḥ saha .. 28 ..
5.101.d:
एवमुक्त्वा रघुश्रेष्ठो राक्षसेन्द्रं विभीषणम् ..
दशरात्रं तत्र तस्थौ लंकायां वानरैः सह .. 28 ..
5.101.m: Having spoken thus to Vibhīṣaṇa, the lord of Rākṣasas, / that best of the Raghus stayed there in Laṅkā for ten nights along with the monkeys,

5.101.s:
kurvanyuddhakathāścitrā yāḥ kṛtāḥ pūrvameva hi ..
paśyanyuddhasya sarvāṇi sthānāni vividhāni ca .. 29 ..
5.101.d:
कुर्वन्युद्धकथाश्चित्रा याः कृताः पूर्वमेव हि ..
पश्यन्युद्धस्य सर्वाणि स्थानानि विविधानि च .. 29 ..
5.101.m: recounting varied tales of the battle that had indeed been fought previously, / and viewing all the various locations of the battle,

5.101.s:
śaṃsamānaḥ pravīrāṃstānrākṣasānbalavattarān ..
kumbhakarṇendrajitpūrvānsaṃkhye cābhimukhāgatān .. 6.101.30 ..
5.101.d:
शंसमानः प्रवीरांस्तान्राक्षसान्बलवत्तरान् ..
कुम्भकर्णेन्द्रजित्पूर्वान्संख्ये चाभिमुखागतान् .. 6.101.30 ..
5.101.m: praising those mighty champions among the Rākṣasas, / Kumbhakarṇa, Indrajit, and others, who had faced him in battle.

5.101.s:
tataścaikādaśe prāpte divase raghunaṃdanaḥ ..
puṣpakaṃ tatsamāruhya prasthitaḥ svapurīṃ prati .. 31 ..
5.101.d:
ततश्चैकादशे प्राप्ते दिवसे रघुनंदनः ..
पुष्पकं तत्समारुह्य प्रस्थितः स्वपुरीं प्रति .. 31 ..
5.101.m: And then, when the eleventh day arrived, the delight of the Raghus, / having mounted that Puṣpaka [vimāna], set out towards his own city.

5.101.s:
vānaraistaiḥ samopeto vibhīṣaṇapuraḥsaraḥ ..
tataḥ saṃsthāpayāmāsa setuprāṃte maheśvaram .. 32
5.101.d:
वानरैस्तैः समोपेतो विभीषणपुरःसरः ..
ततः संस्थापयामास सेतुप्रांते महेश्वरम् .. 32
5.101.m: Accompanied by those monkeys, preceded by Vibhīṣaṇa, / he then installed Maheśvara at the end of the bridge.

5.101.s:
madhye caiva tathādau ca śraddhāpūtena cetasā ..
rāmeśvaratrayaṃ rāma evaṃ tatra vidhāya saḥ .. 33 ..
5.101.d:
मध्ये चैव तथादौ च श्रद्धापूतेन चेतसा ..
रामेश्वरत्रयं राम एवं तत्र विधाय सः .. 33 ..
5.101.m: And in the middle and also at the beginning, with a mind purified by faith, / having thus established three Rāmeśvara [liṅgas] there, Rāma,

5.101.s:
setubaṃdhaṃ tathāsādya prasthitaḥ svagṛhaṃ prati ..
tāvadvibhīṣaṇenoktaḥ praṇipatya muhurmuhuḥ .. 34 ..
5.101.d:
सेतुबंधं तथासाद्य प्रस्थितः स्वगृहं प्रति ..
तावद्विभीषणेनोक्तः प्रणिपत्य मुहुर्मुहुः .. 34 ..
5.101.m: having reached the causeway, set out toward his home. / Then he was addressed by Vibhīṣaṇa, bowing repeatedly:

5.101.s:
.. vibhīṣaṇa uvāca .. ..
anena setumārgeṇa rāmeśvaradidṛkṣayā ..
mānavā āgamiṣyaṃti kautukācchraddhayāvitāḥ .. 35 ..
5.101.d:
.. विभीषण उवाच .. ..
अनेन सेतुमार्गेण रामेश्वरदिदृक्षया ..
मानवा आगमिष्यंति कौतुकाच्छ्रद्धयाविताः .. 35 ..
5.101.m: Vibhīṣaṇa said: / By this causeway path, desiring to see Rāmeśvara, / men will come out of curiosity, endowed with faith.

5.101.s:
rākṣasānāṃ mahārāja jātiḥ krūratamā matā ..
dṛṣṭvā mānuṣamāyāṃtaṃ māṃsasyecchā prajāyate .. 36 ..
5.101.d:
राक्षसानां महाराज जातिः क्रूरतमा मता ..
दृष्ट्वा मानुषमायांतं मांसस्येच्छा प्रजायते .. 36 ..
5.101.m: O great king, the race of rākṣasas is considered most cruel. / Upon seeing a human approaching, a desire for flesh arises.

5.101.s:
yadā kaścijjanaṃ kaścidrākṣaso bhakṣayiṣyati .
ājñābhaṃgo dhruvaṃ bhāvī mama bhaktiratasya ca .. 37 ..
5.101.d:
यदा कश्चिज्जनं कश्चिद्राक्षसो भक्षयिष्यति .
आज्ञाभंगो ध्रुवं भावी मम भक्तिरतस्य च .. 37 ..
5.101.m: When some rākṣasa eats some person, / there will surely be a violation of my command, devoted to devotion though I am.

5.101.s:
bhaviṣyaṃti kalau kāle daridrā nṛpamānavāḥ ..
te'tra svarṇasya lobhena devatādarśanāya ca .. 38 ..
5.101.d:
भविष्यंति कलौ काले दरिद्रा नृपमानवाः ..
तेऽत्र स्वर्णस्य लोभेन देवतादर्शनाय च .. 38 ..
5.101.m: In the Kali age, kings and men will be poor; / they will [come] here out of greed for gold and for the darśana of the deity,

5.101.s:
nityaṃ caivāgamiṣyanti tyaktvā rakṣaḥkṛtaṃ bhayam .
teṣāṃ yadi vadhaṃ kaścidrākṣasātprāpayiṣyati .. 39 ..
5.101.d:
नित्यं चैवागमिष्यन्ति त्यक्त्वा रक्षःकृतं भयम् .
तेषां यदि वधं कश्चिद्राक्षसात्प्रापयिष्यति .. 39 ..
5.101.m: and they will always come, casting aside the fear caused by rākṣasas. / If someone among them suffers death from a rākṣasa,

5.101.s:
bhaviṣyati ca me doṣaḥ prabhudrohodbhavaḥ prabho ..
tasmātkaṃcidupāyaṃ tvaṃ cintayasva yathā mama .
ājñābhaṃgakṛtaṃ pāpaṃ jāyate na guro kvacit .. 6.101.40 ..
5.101.d:
भविष्यति च मे दोषः प्रभुद्रोहोद्भवः प्रभो ..
तस्मात्कंचिदुपायं त्वं चिन्तयस्व यथा मम .
आज्ञाभंगकृतं पापं जायते न गुरो क्वचित् .. 6.101.40 ..
5.101.m: then the fault arising from treason against my lord will fall upon me, O Lord. / Therefore, devise some means so that / the sin caused by violation of command may never arise for me, O Guru.

5.101.s:
tasya tadvacanaṃ śrutvā tataḥ sa raghusattamaḥ ..
bāḍhamityeva coktvātha cāpaṃ sajjīcakāra saḥ ... .. 41 ..
5.101.d:
तस्य तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा ततः स रघुसत्तमः ..
बाढमित्येव चोक्त्वाथ चापं सज्जीचकार सः ... .. 41 ..
5.101.m: Having heard those words of his, that best of the Raghus, / saying, “So be it,” then readied his bow.

5.101.s:
tatastaṃ kīrtirūpaṃ ca madhyadeśe raghūttamaḥ..
acchinanniśitairbāṇairdaśayojanavistṛtam.. 42 ..
5.101.d:
ततस्तं कीर्तिरूपं च मध्यदेशे रघूत्तमः..
अच्छिनन्निशितैर्बाणैर्दशयोजनविस्तृतम्.. 42 ..
5.101.m: Then that best of the Raghus cut through that [causeway], which was the embodiment of his fame, in the middle / for an extent of ten yojanas with sharp arrows.

5.101.s:
tena saṃsthāpito yatra śikhare śaṃkaraḥ svayam...
śikharaṃ tatsaliṃgaṃ ca patitaṃ vāridherjale .. 43 ..
5.101.d:
तेन संस्थापितो यत्र शिखरे शंकरः स्वयम्...
शिखरं तत्सलिंगं च पतितं वारिधेर्जले .. 43 ..
5.101.m: The peak where Śaṃkara had been installed by him himself— / that peak along with the liṅga fell into the water of the ocean.

5.101.s:
evaṃ mārgamagamyaṃ taṃ kṛtvā setusamudbhavam ..
vānarai rākṣasaiḥ sārdhaṃ tataḥ saṃprasthito gṛham .. 44 ...
5.101.d:
एवं मार्गमगम्यं तं कृत्वा सेतुसमुद्भवम् ..
वानरै राक्षसैः सार्धं ततः संप्रस्थितो गृहम् .. 44 ...
5.101.m: Having thus rendered that path across the causeway impassable, / he then departed for home together with the monkeys and the rākṣasas.

5.101.s: iti śrīskāṃde mahāpurāṇaekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ ṣaṣṭhe nāgarakhaṇḍe hāṭakeśvarakṣetramāhātmye setumadhye śrīrāmakṛtarāmeśvarapratiṣṭhāvarṇanaṃnāmaiko ttaraśatatamo'dhyāyaḥ .. 101 ..
5.101.d: इति श्रीस्कांदे महापुराणएकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां षष्ठे नागरखण्डे हाटकेश्वरक्षेत्रमाहात्म्ये सेतुमध्ये श्रीरामकृतरामेश्वरप्रतिष्ठावर्णनंनामैको त्तरशततमोऽध्यायः .. 101 ..
5.101.m: Thus ends the one hundred and first chapter, named “Description of the Consecration of Rāmeśvara in the Middle of the Causeway by Śrī Rāma,” in the Māhātmya of the Hāṭakeśvara Kṣetra in the sixth section, the Nāgarakhaṇḍa, of the glorious Skandapurāṇa, a collection of eighty-one thousand verses.

5.102.s:
.. sūta uvāca .. ..
saṃprasthitasya rāmasya svakīyaṃ sadanaṃ prati ..
yadāścaryamabhūnmārge śrūyatāṃ dvijasattamāḥ .. 1 ..
5.102.d:
.. सूत उवाच .. ..
संप्रस्थितस्य रामस्य स्वकीयं सदनं प्रति ..
यदाश्चर्यमभून्मार्गे श्रूयतां द्विजसत्तमाः .. 1 ..
5.102.m: Sūta said: / As Rāma set out toward his own abode, / hear, O best of the twice-born, the wonder that occurred on the way.

5.102.s:
nabhomārgeṇa gacchattadvimānaṃ puṣpakaṃ dvijāḥ ..
akasmādeva sañjātaṃ niścalaṃ citrakṛnnṛṇām .. 2 ..
5.102.d:
नभोमार्गेण गच्छत्तद्विमानं पुष्पकं द्विजाः ..
अकस्मादेव सञ्जातं निश्चलं चित्रकृन्नृणाम् .. 2 ..
5.102.m: O twice-born, that aerial chariot Puṣpaka going along the skyway / suddenly became motionless, causing wonder to men.

5.102.s:
atha tanniścalaṃ dṛṣṭvā puṣpakaṃ gaganāṃgaṇe ..
rāmo vāyusutasyedaṃ vacanaṃ prāha vismayāt .. 3
5.102.d:
अथ तन्निश्चलं दृष्ट्वा पुष्पकं गगनांगणे ..
रामो वायुसुतस्येदं वचनं प्राह विस्मयात् .. 3
5.102.m: Then, seeing that Puṣpaka motionless in the courtyard of the sky, / Rāma in astonishment spoke these words to the son of the wind:

5.102.s:
tvaṃ gatvā mārute śīghraṃ bhūmiṃ jānīhi kāraṇam ..
kimetatpuṣpakaṃ vyomni niścalatvamupāgatam .. 4 ..
5.102.d:
त्वं गत्वा मारुते शीघ्रं भूमिं जानीहि कारणम् ..
किमेतत्पुष्पकं व्योम्नि निश्चलत्वमुपागतम् .. 4 ..
5.102.m: O son of the wind, go quickly to the earth and ascertain the reason: / why has this Puṣpaka become motionless in the sky?

5.102.s:
kadāciddhāryate nāsya gatiḥ kutrāpi kenacit ..
brahmadṛṣṭiprasūtasya puṣpakasya mahātmanaḥ .. 5 ..
5.102.d:
कदाचिद्धार्यते नास्य गतिः कुत्रापि केनचित् ..
ब्रह्मदृष्टिप्रसूतस्य पुष्पकस्य महात्मनः .. 5 ..
5.102.m: Its movement has never anywhere been checked by anyone, / this noble Puṣpaka born of the glance of Brahmā.

5.102.s:
bāḍhamityeva sa procya hanūmāndharaṇītalam ..
gatvā śīghraṃ punaḥ prāha praṇipatya raghūttamam .. 6 ..
5.102.d:
बाढमित्येव स प्रोच्य हनूमान्धरणीतलम् ..
गत्वा शीघ्रं पुनः प्राह प्रणिपत्य रघूत्तमम् .. 6 ..
5.102.m: Saying “So be it,” Hanūmān went to the surface of the earth, / and returning quickly, bowed to the best of the Raghus and spoke:

5.102.s:
atrāsyādhaḥ śubhaṃ kṣetraṃ hāṭakeśvara saṃjñitam ..
yatra sākṣājjagatkartā svayaṃ brahmā vyavasthitaḥ .. 7 ..
5.102.d:
अत्रास्याधः शुभं क्षेत्रं हाटकेश्वर संज्ञितम् ..
यत्र साक्षाज्जगत्कर्ता स्वयं ब्रह्मा व्यवस्थितः .. 7 ..
5.102.m: Here beneath this is the auspicious sacred field named Hāṭakeśvara, / where Brahmā himself, the creator of the world, resides in person.

5.102.s:
ādityā vasavo rudrā devavaidyau tathāśvinau ..
tatra tiṣṭhanti te sarve tathānye siddhakinnarāḥ .. 8 ..
5.102.d:
आदित्या वसवो रुद्रा देववैद्यौ तथाश्विनौ ..
तत्र तिष्ठन्ति ते सर्वे तथान्ये सिद्धकिन्नराः .. 8 ..
5.102.m: The Ādityas, the Vasus, the Rudras, the two divine physicians the Aśvins, / they all stay there, as well as other siddhas and kinnaras.

5.102.s:
etasmātkāraṇānnaitadatikrāmati puṣpakam ..
tatkṣetraṃ niścalībhūtaṃ satyametanmayoditam .. 9 ..
5.102.d:
एतस्मात्कारणान्नैतदतिक्रामति पुष्पकम् ..
तत्क्षेत्रं निश्चलीभूतं सत्यमेतन्मयोदितम् .. 9 ..
5.102.m: For this reason, this Puṣpaka does not cross over / that sacred field and has become motionless; this which I have said is true.

5.102.s:
.. sūta uvāca .. ..
tasya tadvacanaṃ śrutvā kautūhalasamavitaḥ ..
puṣpakaṃ prerayāmāsa tatkṣetraṃ prati rāghavaḥ ..6.102.....
sarvaistairvānaraiḥ sārdhaṃ rākṣasaiśca pṛthagvidhaiḥ ..
avatīrya tato hṛṣṭastasminkṣetre samantataḥ .. 11 ..
5.102.d:
.. सूत उवाच .. ..
तस्य तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा कौतूहलसमवितः ..
पुष्पकं प्रेरयामास तत्क्षेत्रं प्रति राघवः ..6.102.....
सर्वैस्तैर्वानरैः सार्धं राक्षसैश्च पृथग्विधैः ..
अवतीर्य ततो हृष्टस्तस्मिन्क्षेत्रे समन्ततः .. 11 ..
5.102.m: Sūta said: / Having heard those words of his, filled with curiosity, / the descendant of Raghu directed the Puṣpaka toward that sacred field. / Together with all those monkeys and rākṣasas of various kinds, / having descended delighted, he [went] all around that sacred field.

5.102.s:
tīrthamālokayāmāsa puṇyānyāyatanāni ca ..
tato vilokayāmāsa pitāmahavinirmitām ..
cāmuṇḍāṃ tatra ca snātvā kuṇḍe kāmapradāyini .. 12 ..
5.102.d:
तीर्थमालोकयामास पुण्यान्यायतनानि च ..
ततो विलोकयामास पितामहविनिर्मिताम् ..
चामुण्डां तत्र च स्नात्वा कुण्डे कामप्रदायिनि .. 12 ..
5.102.m: He looked at the sacred ford and the holy shrines. / Then he beheld Cāmuṇḍā fashioned by the Grandfather, / having bathed there in the pool that grants desires.

5.102.s:
tato vilokayāmāsa pitrā tasya vinirmitam..
rāmaḥ svamiva deveśaṃ dṛṣṭvā devaṃ caturbhujam.. .. 13 ..
5.102.d:
ततो विलोकयामास पित्रा तस्य विनिर्मितम्..
रामः स्वमिव देवेशं दृष्ट्वा देवं चतुर्भुजम्.. .. 13 ..
5.102.m: Then Rāma beheld [the image] fashioned by his father, / having seen the four-armed god, the lord of deities, as if his own self.

5.102.s:
rājavāpyāṃ śucirbhūtvā snātvā tarpya nijānpitṝn ..
tataśca cintayāmāsa kṣetre tra bahupuṇyade .. 14 ..
5.102.d:
राजवाप्यां शुचिर्भूत्वा स्नात्वा तर्प्य निजान्पितॄन् ..
ततश्च चिन्तयामास क्षेत्रे त्र बहुपुण्यदे .. 14 ..
5.102.m: Having become pure and bathed in the king's stepwell, and offered libations to his ancestors, / he then reflected in this sacred field that grants much merit:

5.102.s:
liṃgaṃ saṃsthāpayāmyeva yadvattātena keśavaḥ ..
tathā me dayito bhrātā lakṣmaṇo divamāśritaḥ .. 15 ..
5.102.d:
लिंगं संस्थापयाम्येव यद्वत्तातेन केशवः ..
तथा मे दयितो भ्राता लक्ष्मणो दिवमाश्रितः .. 15 ..
5.102.m: “I shall certainly establish a liṅga, just as Keśava [was established] by my father. / Likewise, my beloved brother Lakṣmaṇa has resorted to heaven;

5.102.s:
yastasya nāmanirdiṣṭaṃ liṃgaṃ saṃsthāpayāmyaham ..
taṃ cāpi mūrtimaṃtaṃ ca sītayā sahitaṃ śubham ..
kṣetre medhyatame cātra tathātmānaṃ dṛṣanmayam .. 16 ..
5.102.d:
यस्तस्य नामनिर्दिष्टं लिंगं संस्थापयाम्यहम् ..
तं चापि मूर्तिमंतं च सीतया सहितं शुभम् ..
क्षेत्रे मेध्यतमे चात्र तथात्मानं दृषन्मयम् .. 16 ..
5.102.m: I shall establish a liṅga designated with his name. / And [I shall establish] him in sculpted form, and the auspicious [one] accompanied by Sītā, / and likewise myself in stone in this most pure sacred field.”

5.102.s:
evaṃ sa niścayaṃ kṛtvā prāsādānāṃ ca paṃcakam ..
sthāpayāmāsa sadbhaktyā rāmaḥ śastrabhṛtāṃ varaḥ .. 17 ..
5.102.d:
एवं स निश्चयं कृत्वा प्रासादानां च पंचकम् ..
स्थापयामास सद्भक्त्या रामः शस्त्रभृतां वरः .. 17 ..
5.102.m: Having thus resolved, Rāma, the best of weapon-bearers, / established five temples with true devotion.

5.102.s:
tataste vānarāḥ sarve rākṣasāśca viśeṣataḥ ..
liṃgāni sthāpayāmāsuḥ svānisvāni pṛthakpṛthak .. 18 ..
5.102.d:
ततस्ते वानराः सर्वे राक्षसाश्च विशेषतः ..
लिंगानि स्थापयामासुः स्वानिस्वानि पृथक्पृथक् .. 18 ..
5.102.m: Then all those monkeys, and especially the rākṣasas, / established their own respective liṅgas separately.

5.102.s:
tatraiva suciraṃ kālaṃ sthitāste śraddhayā'nvitāḥ ..
tato jagmurayodhyāyāṃ vimānavaramāśritāḥ .. 19 ..
5.102.d:
तत्रैव सुचिरं कालं स्थितास्ते श्रद्धयाऽन्विताः ..
ततो जग्मुरयोध्यायां विमानवरमाश्रिताः .. 19 ..
5.102.m: They remained right there for a very long time, filled with faith; / then, boarding the excellent aerial chariot, they went to Ayodhyā.

5.102.s:
etadvaḥ sarvamākhyātaṃ yathā rāmeśvaro mahān ..
lakṣmaṇeśvarasaṃyuktastasmiṃstīrthe suśobhane .. 6.102.20 ..
5.102.d:
एतद्वः सर्वमाख्यातं यथा रामेश्वरो महान् ..
लक्ष्मणेश्वरसंयुक्तस्तस्मिंस्तीर्थे सुशोभने .. 6.102.20 ..
5.102.m: All this has been related to you: how the great Rāmeśvara / along with Lakṣmaṇeśvara came to be in that very auspicious sacred ford.

5.102.s:
yastau prātaḥ samutthāya sadā paśyati mānavaḥ ..
sa kṛtsnaṃ phalamāpnoti śrute rāmāyaṇe'tra yat .. 21 ..
5.102.d:
यस्तौ प्रातः समुत्थाय सदा पश्यति मानवः ..
स कृत्स्नं फलमाप्नोति श्रुते रामायणेऽत्र यत् .. 21 ..
5.102.m: The person who, having risen in the morning, always sees the two of them, / obtains the entire fruit that is gained here when the Rāmāyaṇa is heard.

5.102.s:
athāṣṭamyāṃ caturdaśyāṃ yo rāmacaritaṃ paṭhet ..
tadagre vājimedhasya sa kṛtsnaṃ labhate phalam .. 22 ..
5.102.d:
अथाष्टम्यां चतुर्दश्यां यो रामचरितं पठेत् ..
तदग्रे वाजिमेधस्य स कृत्स्नं लभते फलम् .. 22 ..
5.102.m: Moreover, whoever recites the deeds of Rāma on the eighth or fourteenth day [of the fortnight] / before them, obtains the full fruit of a horse sacrifice.

5.102.s: iti śrīskāṃde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ ṣaṣṭhe nāgarakhaṇḍe hāṭakeśvarakṣetramāhātmye śrīrāmacandreṇa hāṭakeśvarakṣetre lakṣmaṇādiprāsādapañcakanirmāṇapratiṣṭhāpanavarṇanaṃnāma dvyuttaraśatatamo'dhyāyaḥ .. 102 ..
5.102.d: इति श्रीस्कांदे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां षष्ठे नागरखण्डे हाटकेश्वरक्षेत्रमाहात्म्ये श्रीरामचन्द्रेण हाटकेश्वरक्षेत्रे लक्ष्मणादिप्रासादपञ्चकनिर्माणप्रतिष्ठापनवर्णनंनाम द्व्युत्तरशततमोऽध्यायः .. 102 ..
5.102.m: Thus ends the one hundred and second chapter, named “Description of the Construction and Consecration of the Five Temples Beginning with Lakṣmaṇa by Śrī Rāmacandra in the Hāṭakeśvara Kṣetra,” in the Māhātmya of the Hāṭakeśvara Kṣetra in the sixth section, the Nāgarakhaṇḍa, of the glorious Skandapurāṇa, a collection of eighty-one thousand verses.
